questions.q: Q.1) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Austria 2️⃣ Hungary 3️⃣ Italy 4️⃣ Serbia 5️⃣ Slovenia 6️⃣ Bosnia and Herzegovina How many of the above countries share land borders with Croatia?
questions.e: Croatia is a crescent-shaped country in the northwestern Balkan Peninsula. It shares land borders with Serbia to the east, and Hungary and Slovenia to the north. It also shares a long land border with Bosnia and Herzegovina. Montenegro touches its southern end. Italy shares only a maritime border, not a land border, and Austria does not share any border with Croatia. Therefore, only four of the listed countries (Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina) share land borders. The Danube River separates Croatia from Serbia, while several other rivers like the Kupa and Sutla separate it from Slovenia .

questions.q: Q.2) Which one of the following best describes the term "thirstwave"?
o: A sudden drop in groundwater levels due to over-extraction
Three or more consecutive days of abnormally high evaporative demand
The total amount of water lost by a crop during its growth cycle
An extended heatwave with temperatures exceeding 50°C
questions.e: A "thirstwave" is defined as three or more consecutive days of intense evaporative demand that exceeds the 90th percentile for a specific location and season. Evaporative demand is essentially a measure of how "thirsty" the atmosphere is, representing the potential amount of water it can draw from soil and plants. Unlike standard heatwaves driven by temperature, a thirstwave is influenced by a combination of temperature, humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation. These factors alter the dynamics of land-atmosphere water exchange. In India, this phenomenon is increasingly relevant to agriculture and water management, though there is currently a gap in monitoring these trends .

questions.q: Q.3) Consider the following statements with regard to the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA): 1️⃣ It covers trade in goods only. 2️⃣ It has been ratified by all Parties, except Cambodia. 3️⃣ Under the AITIGA, ASEAN and India have committed to liberalising tariffs on over 90 per cent of goods.
questions.e: The AITIGA, signed in 2009 and effective from January 1, 2010, specifically covers trade in goods only and does not include services. Under this agreement, ASEAN and India committed to liberalising tariffs on over 90 percent of goods and progressively eliminating duties on 76.4 percent of goods. Statement II is incorrect because while the separate Trade in Services Agreement (signed in 2014) has been ratified by all parties, the prompt refers to AITIGA. The agreement allows longer timeframes for less developed ASEAN members like Myanmar and Laos to reduce tariffs. It created one of the world's largest free trade areas .

questions.q: Q.4) Consider the following: 1️⃣ NAVYA 2️⃣ Sabla 3️⃣ Saksham 4️⃣ Kishori Shakti Yojana 5️⃣ Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan How many of the above initiatives in India have been launched specifically for adolescent girls?
questions.e: Three of the listed initiatives are specifically for adolescent girls. NAVYA is a pilot vocational training program for girls aged 16-18. Sabla (Rajiv Gandhi Scheme for Empowerment of Adolescent Girls) targets girls aged 11-18 to improve nutrition, health, and life skills. Kishori Shakti Yojana also supports the holistic development and nutritional needs of girls aged 11-18. Saksham is actually an AICTE scheme to support specially-abled children in technical education. Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan is focused on overall accessibility for persons with disabilities rather than specifically targeting adolescent girls .

questions.q: Q.5) Consider the following statements with regard to the Himalayan Brown Bears: 1️⃣ They hibernate through most of the winter, relying on stored body fat to survive. 2️⃣ They are typically found above the tree line, between 3,000 and 5,500 metres. 3️⃣ They are endemic to Gangotri National Park.
questions.e: Himalayan brown bears (Ursus arctos isabellinus) are found at high altitudes between 3,000 and 5,500 meters, typically above the tree line. They hibernate starting around October and can lose up to one-third of their body weight by spring. While they are found in Gangotri National Park, they are not endemic to it; their range extends across Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and parts of Pakistan. They are solitary, diurnal, and omnivorous, feeding on roots, insects, and small mammals like marmots. Their recent sighting in areas like Dumka is seen as a sign of potential range expansion .

questions.q: Q.6) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Treasury Bills 2️⃣ Preference shares 3️⃣ Government Securities 4️⃣ Bonds How many of the above investment instruments are components of a Debt Mutual Fund?
questions.e: A Debt Mutual Fund primarily invests in fixed-income instruments. Components include Treasury Bills (T-Bills), which are short-term government loans , Government Securities (G-Secs), which are long-term government loans , and Bonds issued by companies or the government. Preference shares are not typically included in these funds as they are a special type of share where dividends are paid before common stock dividends, rather than being a standard debt instrument. These funds aim to provide steady returns with relatively lower risk compared to equity funds .

questions.q: Q.7) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Falkland: South Atlantic Ocean 2️⃣ Chios: North Sea 3️⃣ Kariyachalli: South China Sea How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only the first pair is correctly matched. The Falkland Islands are a UK overseas territory in the South Atlantic Ocean. Chios is a Greek island located in the Aegean Sea, not the North Sea; it is known for exports of mastic gum. Kariyachalli Island is located in the Gulf of Mannar along the southeastern coast of India, part of an ecologically sensitive marine national park, not the South China Sea. Kariyachalli is uninhabited and has faced significant submergence due to rising sea levels and coastal erosion .

questions.q: Q.8) The Nuvvuagittuq Greenstone Belt, believed to contain some of the Earth's oldest rocks, is located in:
questions.e: The Nuvvuagittuq Greenstone Belt is located in Quebec, Canada. Research suggests it contains some of the oldest surviving fragments of Earth's crust, with some rocks dating back 4.16 billion years to the Hadean Eon. While it contains very old rocks (at least 3.75 billion years old), the distinction of the oldest known geological formation is usually given to the Acasta Gneiss Complex in northwestern Canada, which is dated to approximately 4.03 billion years. This age represents the transition between the Hadean and Archean Eons .

questions.q: Q.9) Consider the following statements with respect to Cardamom production in India: 1️⃣ It is native to the forests of the Western Ghats. 2️⃣ Black cardamom is dried with the help of a fire pit, while green cardamom is harvested before it reaches maturity. 3️⃣ Kerala contributes more than half of India's cardamom production.
questions.e: Cardamom, the "Queen of Spices," is native to the rainy forests of the Western Ghats in South India. India's entire production comes from Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, with Kerala alone contributing about 70%. Black cardamom is typically dried using a fire pit, whereas green cardamom is harvested before it reaches full maturity. Ideal conditions for cultivation include loamy acidic soil, thick shade, and elevations between 600 and 1500 meters. Recent investigations have raised concerns about pesticide overuse in Indian spice production .

questions.q: Q.10) The Black Mass Recovery Technology, sometimes seen in the news, is primarily used for:
o: extracting rare earth metals from deep-sea mining
processing industrial slag to extract residual metals
capturing carbon emissions from thermal power plants
recovering valuable metals from end-of-life lithium-ion batteries
questions.e: Black Mass Recovery Technology is a sustainable, indigenous battery recycling process developed to recover battery-grade metals like lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese from end-of-life lithium-ion batteries. It uses a low-temperature, low-pressure hydrometallurgical process that is effective across various battery chemistries, achieving recovery rates of 97-99%. This technology helps reduce India's dependence on imported critical minerals and recycling equipment. The Department of Science & Technology (DST) is currently funding the project to commercialize this end-to-end recycling process .

questions.q: Q.11) Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary, recently declared as India's first Butterfly Sanctuary, is located in which of the following states?
questions.e: The Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary, now officially renamed the Aralam Butterfly Sanctuary, is located in Kerala. Spanning 55 square kilometers on the western slopes of the Western Ghats, it hosts over 266 butterfly species, representing more than 80% of Kerala's total butterfly diversity. The sanctuary is famous for a seasonal migration between December and February involving species like the Common Albatross. Its high biodiversity and the presence of many endemic and endangered species led to its designation as India's first butterfly sanctuary .

questions.q: Q.12) A unique narrative sculpture depicting Lord Shiva's Pralaya Tandava, along with Khadga Ravana seated on Goddess Mari, was recently found at which of the following heritage sites?
questions.e: This unique 15th-century bronze lamp sculpture was discovered at the Anantapadmanabha Temple in Perdoor, Udupi district, Karnataka. One side of the lamp features Lord Shiva performing the Pralaya Tandava (dance of destruction), accompanied by figures like Parvati, Ganapati, and Khadga Ravana seated on Goddess Mari. The other side depicts Lord Vishnu (Anantapadmanabha) being approached by gods to calm Shiva's fury, representing Vaishnava-Shaiva syncretism. Epigraphy confirms the lamp was donated in 1456 CE .

questions.q: Q.13) With reference to the Registration of Births and Deaths in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ All birth and death registrations shall be done only through a centralised portal maintained by the Union Government. 2️⃣ The digital birth certificate serves as the sole valid document for establishing the date of birth for admission to educational institutions.
questions.e: Amendments to the Registration of Births and Deaths (RBD) Act in 2023 mandate that all births and deaths must be registered on the Centre's centralized portal starting October 1, 2023. Since that date, the digital birth certificate has become the single document required to prove the date of birth for various services, including school admissions, government jobs, and marriage registration. The centralized database created through this process is also used to update other records like the National Population Register (NPR) and electoral rolls .

questions.q: Q.14) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Ammonium sulphate 2️⃣ Ozone 3️⃣ Carbon monoxide 4️⃣ Lead How many of the above are secondary pollutants?
questions.e: Secondary pollutants are formed in the atmosphere through chemical reactions, while primary pollutants are emitted directly from sources. Ammonium sulphate is a secondary pollutant formed from the reaction of sulphur dioxide and ammonia. Ozone is also a secondary pollutant formed by reactions in the lower atmosphere. Carbon monoxide and lead are primary pollutants emitted directly from vehicle exhausts and industrial processes. A 2024 study found that secondary pollutants like ammonium sulphate contribute to about one-third of India's PM2.5 levels .

questions.q: Q.15) Recently, Bacillus ayatagriensis bacterium was isolated from the rhizosphere of mulberry plants. In context to this, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It possesses antimicrobial activity and promotes seed germination. 2️⃣ It is widely adopted in organic farming to replace chemical fertilizers and pesticides.
questions.e: Bacillus ayatagriensis is a newly discovered soil bacterium isolated from the rhizosphere of mulberry plants. It has shown strong antimicrobial activity against soil pathogens and significantly enhances seed germination, making it a promising plant growth-promoting microorganism. However, statement II is incorrect because there is no evidence of its "widespread adoption" yet; practical field deployment and regulatory approvals are still pending after the initial research. It is currently positioned as a potential tool for future eco-friendly agriculture .

questions.q: Q.16) The UN80 Initiative, launched in 2024, primarily aims to:
o: streamline UN operations and enhance its relevance in a changing world
improve coordination among UN agencies for delivering humanitarian aid
expand UN peacekeeping operations in conflict zones
reorganise the UN Security Council's membership
questions.e: The UN80 Initiative is a system-wide reform effort launched in preparation for the United Nations' 80th anniversary in 2025. Its primary goal is to streamline operations, sharpen the organization's impact, and reaffirm its relevance in a world facing climate disasters, inequality, and technological disruptions. It also aims to restore global trust in multilateral cooperation, which has weakened due to political disagreements and funding issues. The initiative is a push to make the UN more effective in responding to modern global challenges .

questions.q: Q.17) With reference to satellite-based navigation systems, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ GPS jamming involves a device transmitting signals on the same frequencies used by GPS satellites. 2️⃣ GPS spoofing refers to the deliberate emission of strong radio signals to disrupt the reception of satellite signals.
questions.e: Both statements are incorrect because the definitions are swapped. GPS jamming involves emitting strong radio signals to overpower and disrupt GPS frequencies, making receivers unable to determine location. GPS spoofing involves transmitting false signals on the same frequencies to deceive a receiver into trusting incorrect data. While both are deliberate cyber-attacks on navigation systems, jamming entirely blocks the signal, whereas spoofing tricks the system with wrong information. These interferences critically threaten global air and maritime safety .

questions.q: Q.18) The drug 'Lenacapavir', recently seen in the news, is used for the prevention of:
questions.e: Lenacapavir is a groundbreaking antiretroviral drug recently approved as a Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) to prevent HIV infection. It is unique because it is an injectable drug administered only twice a year, providing long-acting protection. Clinical studies show it is 99.9% effective in preventing HIV transmission. PrEP is intended for HIV-negative individuals at high risk, such as sex workers or serodiscordant couples. In India, NACO has been piloting PrEP since 2021, and there is a growing focus on incorporating long-acting options like Lenacapavir .

questions.q: Q.19) Which of the following statements is/are correct with respect to the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV): 1️⃣ It uses a liquid propulsion-based Velocity Trimming Module (VTM) for all three stages. 2️⃣ It is capable of launching a satellite of less than 500 kg in a Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
questions.e: The SSLV is a three-stage rocket configured with three solid propulsion stages and uses a liquid-based Velocity Trimming Module (VTM) only as a terminal stage, not for all three stages. It is designed to launch satellites weighing up to 500 kg into a 500 km Low Earth Orbit (LEO). Key advantages include low cost, quick turnaround time, and minimal launch infrastructure requirements. Recently, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) won the bid to commercialize SSLV technology from ISRO to boost private sector participation in space .

questions.q: Q.20) Consider the following statements with regard to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT): 1️⃣ It is the only legally binding multilateral agreement that is committed to the goal of nuclear disarmament. 2️⃣ It recognises only five countries as nuclear-weapon States. 3️⃣ It establishes a safeguards system under the responsibility of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).
questions.e: The NPT is the only legally binding multilateral commitment to nuclear disarmament by nuclear-weapon states. It recognizes only the five countries that tested weapons before 1967 (US, Russia, UK, France, China) as nuclear-weapon states. It also establishes a safeguards system managed by the IAEA to verify compliance through inspections. India and Pakistan have not signed the treaty, arguing it creates a discriminatory framework. The treaty has 191 member states and was extended indefinitely in 1995 .

questions.q: Q.21) When the Reserve Bank of India adopts an accommodative monetary policy stance, it primarily aims to:
o: encourage capital inflows to stabilize the rupee
promote credit growth and support economic expansion
increase interest rates to control inflation
tighten monetary conditions to curb excess demand
questions.e: An accommodative stance indicates that the central bank is prepared to expand the money supply to support economic growth. During this phase, the RBI is generally inclined to lower interest rates to encourage credit growth, and rate hikes are effectively ruled out. This stance is typically adopted when the economy needs a stimulus and inflation is not an immediate threat. In contrast, a "neutral" stance means the bank can either cut or increase rates, while "calibrated tightening" indicates that rate cuts are off the table .

questions.q: Q.22) Which of the following are the features of the "NAKSHATRA" facility developed in India? 1️⃣ Optimise the data pipeline for genomic research 2️⃣ Strengthening viral genomic surveillance 3️⃣ Enabling faster analysis of genomic data for the early detection of disease threats 4️⃣ Supporting Al-driven efforts in vaccine and drug development
questions.e: NAKSHATRA is a high-performance computing cluster set up by the ICMR at the National Institute of Virology in Pune. It features an optimized genomic data pipeline for large-scale sequencing and research. Its goals include strengthening viral genomic surveillance to prepare for future pandemics and enabling faster analysis of complex data for early threat detection. Additionally, it supports AI-driven efforts in the development of vaccines and drugs to accelerate biomedical research. It was developed under the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission .

questions.q: Q.23) In the context of the Indian banking system, a "mule account" refers to a:
o: bank account used for agricultural subsidies
legitimate account used by criminals to launder illicit money
dormant account with no recent transactions
fraudulent account created using fake documents
questions.e: Mule accounts are bank accounts used to receive and transfer funds derived from illegal activities, facilitating money laundering. Criminals recruit "money mules" to move proceeds from scams, human trafficking, or drug trafficking. There are several types: "Victim Mules" are unaware they are being exploited, "Misled Mules" think they are doing legitimate work, while "Accomplice Mules" are fully aware of the crime. Effective monitoring allows banks to identify and shut down these accounts. The Enforcement Directorate recently seized hundreds of such accounts .

questions.q: Q.24) The Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) has been launched to implement the provisions of which of the following Acts?
o: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
questions.e: DAJGUA is a central scheme used by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to fund structural mechanisms for implementing the Forest Rights Act (FRA) of 2006. Under this scheme, 324 district-level FRA cells have been sanctioned across 18 states and UTs to give forest rights to Scheduled Tribes and forest-dwelling communities. The Union government provides specific grants-in-aid for these cells—8.67 lakh for district cells and 25.85 lakh for state cells. This marks the first time the Union government has directly funded such implementation mechanisms for the FRA .

questions.q: Q.25) The locations Fordow, Isfahan and Natanz, recently seen in the news, are known for:
o: US military bases in the Middle East
strategic oil reserves in Saudi Arabia
questions.e: Fordow, Isfahan, and Natanz are critical sites in Iran's nuclear program, serving as uranium enrichment centers. These facilities use technology to convert natural uranium into Highly Enriched Uranium (HEU), a key component for nuclear weapons. While 3-5% enrichment is used for civilian power, weapons-grade uranium requires 90% or more. These locations were recently targeted in airstrikes. Uranium enrichment increases the proportion of the fissile isotope U-235, which is necessary to sustain a nuclear chain reaction .

questions.q: Q.26) Consider the following statements regarding India Post Payments Banks (IPPBs): 1️⃣ They are a 100% Government of India equity-owned entity. 2️⃣ They cannot accept term deposits and any non-resident Indian deposits. 3️⃣ They cannot set up subsidiaries to undertake non-banking financial services activities. 4️⃣ They are subject to both the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR).
questions.e: IPPB is 100% owned by the Government of India and was launched in 2018 under the Ministry of Communications. As a payments bank, it cannot accept NRI deposits, term deposits (FD/RD), or engage in direct lending. It is also prohibited from setting up subsidiaries for non-banking financial services. However, it must maintain a CRR with the RBI and invest at least 75% of its demand deposits in SLR-eligible government securities. IPPB recently received the Digital Payments Award 2024-25 .

questions.q: Q.27) The "Ottawa Convention", recently seen in the news, aims to:
o: regulate cross-border digital taxation among OECD nations
ban the use of anti-personnel landmines
prohibit the use of cluster munitions in armed conflict
protect the intellectual property rights of indigenous communities
questions.e: The Ottawa Convention, or the Mine Ban Treaty, aims to end the use, stockpiling, production, and transfer of anti-personnel landmines (APLs) worldwide. It does not cover anti-tank mines. While 164 states are parties, major countries like India, the US, and Russia have not joined. Recently, Finland's parliament voted to withdraw from the treaty due to military concerns regarding Russia, joining other Baltic and NATO members in exiting or planning to exit the agreement. The treaty originally entered into force in 1999 .

questions.q: Q.28) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Hormuz: Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman 2️⃣ Bab-el-Mandeb: Red Sea and Gulf of Aden 3️⃣ Gibraltar: Black Sea and Sea of Marmara How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only the first two pairs are correct. The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and is a vital oil transit chokepoint. The Bab-el-Mandeb Strait connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic Ocean, not the Black Sea. It is the Bosphorus Strait that connects the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara, dividing Turkey between Europe and Asia. Iran recently proposed closing the Strait of Hormuz following US strikes .

questions.q: Q.29) Recently, India's first off-grid 5 MW green hydrogen pilot plant was inaugurated at which of the following locations?
questions.e: India's first off-grid 5 MW green hydrogen pilot plant was launched in Kutch, Gujarat. Developed by Adani New Industries Limited (ANIL), the plant is not connected to the main electrical grid and relies entirely on its own renewable energy generation to produce hydrogen through electrolysis. It uses a fully automated "closed-loop" system that adjusts to real-time renewable energy inputs, like shifting solar power, to ensure operational efficiency and safety. This facility represents a major step toward sustainable energy production in India .

questions.q: Q.30) In many Low and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs), substances like chloramphenicol, tylosin and TCN (a mix of oxytetracycline, chloramphenicol and neomycin) continue to be used despite being banned in several developed nations. These substances are used as:
o: antibiotics in livestock and poultry feed
growth enhancers in genetically modified crops
questions.e: These substances are antibiotics used in livestock feed to boost growth and intensify production in LMICs. While banned in developed nations, their use in LMICs is often unregulated. Over-exposure in humans can lead to kidney disease, cancers, and aplastic anaemia. This practice contributes to the growing global concern of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR). India is now encouraging sustainable, climate-resilient insect-based feed as an alternative to reduce environmental impact and combat AMR in poultry and aquaculture .

questions.q: Q.31) Which of the following constitutes the "trifecta" of international science-policy bodies addressing the triple planetary crisis of climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution? 1️⃣ Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) 2️⃣ Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) 3️⃣ Science-Policy Panel on Chemicals, Waste and Pollution 4️⃣ Global Environment Facility (GEF)
questions.e: The "trifecta" consists of the IPCC (climate change), IPBES (biodiversity), and the newly created Science-Policy Panel on Chemicals, Waste and Pollution. This new panel was initiated following a 2022 UN Environment Assembly resolution to strengthen evidence-based decision-making regarding pollution. The Global Environment Facility (GEF) is not a science-policy panel; it is a multilateral financial mechanism established in 1991 to provide grants for environmental projects in developing countries. These three bodies collectively address the "triple planetary crisis" .

questions.q: Q.32) What is the primary purpose of Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) in climate mitigation strategies?
o: Artificially enhance rainfall in arid regions
Increase soil fertility using synthetic fertilizers
Accelerate the natural process of carbon dioxide capture and storage
Reduce ozone depletion by neutralizing CFCs
questions.e: ERW is a climate mitigation strategy that speeds up the natural geological process of removing CO2 from the atmosphere. By spreading finely crushed rocks like basalt across croplands, the surface area is increased, accelerating the reaction where CO2 dissolves into water as carbonic acid and is eventually trapped as limestone in the oceans. This process also increases soil alkalinity, which can boost crop growth and nutrients. Basalt is often used because it is abundant and frequently a byproduct of quarrying, which helps lower costs .

questions.q: Q.33) Candida tropicalis, recently seen in the news, is best described as:
o: a protozoan parasite responsible for malaria resurgence in tropical regions
a fungal pathogen associated with high mortality and resistance to azole drugs
a bacterial pathogen causing respiratory infections
a virus known for causing hemorrhagic fever outbreaks
questions.e: Candida tropicalis is a significant fungal pathogen that has shown high mortality rates of 55-60%. It is becoming a major medical concern due to its increasing resistance to common azole-class antifungal drugs like fluconazole and voriconazole. Researchers have found that resistant strains use chromosome alterations (aneuploidy or ploidy plasticity) to survive drug treatments. These chromosome count differences from the norm allow the fungus to manage managing infections more effectively despite medical interventions .

questions.q: Q.34) Consider the following statements with reference to the State of World Population (SOWP) Report, 2025: 1️⃣ It is published by UNESCO. 2️⃣ More than 60% percent of India's population in the 15-64 age group.
questions.e: The 2025 SOWP Report is published by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), not UNESCO. According to the report, India's population has reached 1.46 billion, with 68 percent of people falling in the 15-64 age group. Replacement-level fertility is 2.1 births per woman, but rates have declined below this in 31 Indian states and UTs. Financial constraints, job insecurity, and housing inadequacy were cited as key deterrents to reproductive autonomy. Higher fertility persists in states like Bihar (3.0) and Uttar Pradesh (2.7) .

questions.q: Q.35) Which of the following countries have recently launched the 'Blue Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC)' challenge'?
o: United States of America and Canada
questions.e: Brazil and France launched the Blue NDC Challenge at the 2025 UN Ocean Conference. This global initiative urges countries to integrate ocean-based climate actions into their national climate plans (NDCs) before COP30. NDCs are the core strategy for nations to cut emissions and limit warming to 1.5°C. The challenge highlights the ocean's role as a natural climate solution and is supported by groups like Ocean Conservancy and the World Resources Institute. It marks a significant recognition of the ocean's power in global climate efforts .

questions.q: Q.36) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Ocean acidification is posing grave threats to marine ecosystems and global climate stability. Statement II: Ocean acidification has breached its planetary boundary.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
questions.e: Statement I is correct because ocean acidification, caused by the ocean absorbing CO2 and forming carbonic acid, harms marine life like corals and plankton, disrupting the food chain and biodiversity. Statement II is also correct; while it was previously believed that this "planetary boundary" had not been crossed, a 2020 study found it was breached approximately five years ago. Human activities like burning fossil fuels are the primary driver of this acidification, and the breach of this safety limit directly contributes to the grave threats mentioned .

questions.q: Q.37) Two Indian astronauts participated in international space missions (1980s and 2020s). In the above context, which of the following statements are correct with regard to the distinguishing features of the latter mission compared to the former? 1️⃣ The recent mission was part of a commercially operated US-based program, while the earlier was a bilateral diplomatic initiative with the USSR. 2️⃣ The earlier mission included a longer duration of stay in space, while the recent mission included more experiments and deeper Indian scientific involvement. 3️⃣ The recent mission marked India's first entry into the ISS, while the earlier one involved a stay aboard a Soviet-era space station.
questions.e: Rakesh Sharma’s 1984 mission was a Soviet-led diplomatic initiative where he spent eight days on the Salyut 7 station. Shubhanshu Shukla’s Axiom-4 mission is a commercial US-based program to the International Space Station (ISS). While Sharma stayed for eight days with 43 sessions, Shukla's mission planned for two weeks with 60 experiments, including seven designed by ISRO. Shukla's mission marks India's first entry into the ISS. Thus, all statements correctly distinguish the contexts, scientific depth, and station types of the two missions .

questions.q: Q.38) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He emphasised personal devotion to God over ritualistic religious practices. 2️⃣ He was associated with key works like Bijak, Sakhi Granth and Anurag Sagar. 3️⃣ His verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib. Who is this personality?
questions.e: Sant Kabir Das was a 15th-century mystic poet and social reformer who questioned ritualistic worship and emphasized personal devotion and critical thinking. His major works include Bijak, Sakhi Granth, Anurag Sagar, and Kabir Granthavali. His teachings advocated for religious harmony and social equality, and his verses were later compiled in the Sikh holy scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib. Born into a unique background reflecting both Hindu and Islamic influences, his "Kabir Ke Dohe" remain popular today. His 648th birth anniversary was recently celebrated .

questions.q: Q.39) With reference to the 'CROPIC Initiative', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is launched by the Ministry of Science and Technology. 2️⃣ It is a part of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. 3️⃣ It will help in crop damage assessment in case of localized calamities.
questions.e: CROPIC was launched by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, not Science and Technology. It is a study under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana that uses field photographs and AI-based models for crop health monitoring. The initiative utilizes a mobile app to collect geotagged photographs from farmers for crop validation and damage assessment during localized calamities. This real-time field data helps in making more accurate decisions regarding insurance and crop management .

questions.q: Q.40) With reference to Eurasian otter, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is usually nocturnal and found in freshwater environments. 2️⃣ It is a herbivorous animal that feeds on aquatic grass. 3️⃣ It is found only in Kashmir Himalayas in India. Which of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: Statements II and III are incorrect. The Eurasian otter has a varied carnivorous diet including fish, crustaceans, amphibians, and sometimes birds or insects. In India, it is not limited to Kashmir; it is also found in the Northern, North Eastern, and Southern parts, recently being spotted in the Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary in Kerala. Statement I is correct: it is elusive, solitary, usually nocturnal, and inhabits freshwater environments, though some populations forage in the sea. It is classified as 'near threatened' by the IUCN .

questions.q: Q.41) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Religious symbols 2️⃣ A vibrant, sophisticated urban society 3️⃣ Port shreds with Tamil Brahmi inscriptions 4️⃣ Graffiti of the sun and moon 5️⃣ An ivory dice How many of the above have been found at Keeladi?
questions.e: Four of the listed items were found at Keeladi. Findings included evidence of a sophisticated urban society with systematic planning, Tamil Brahmi inscriptions on pottery indicating high literacy, graffiti of the sun and moon reflecting astronomical sense, and an ivory dice suggesting an elite society. Most importantly, no religious symbols were found, hinting at a secular civilization. Keeladi is a hamlet in Tamil Nadu where excavations have pushed the Sangam age back to 800 BCE .

questions.q: Q.42) Consider the following statements with reference to the Emperor Penguins: 1️⃣ They are only aquatic mammals in Antarctica. 2️⃣ They are the tallest and heaviest species of penguins. 3️⃣ They exhibit huddling behaviour to protect from cold.
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect because penguins are flightless aquatic birds, not mammals. Statement II is correct; Emperor penguins are the tallest and heaviest species alive today, evolved specifically for harsh Antarctic environments. Statement III is also correct; they exhibit huddling behavior where thousands of birds pack together for warmth. They breed on 'fast ice' during the coldest winter months. Their population was estimated at nearly 600,000 in 2009 .

questions.q: Q.43) Which of the following are the most likely impacts of ocean darkening? 1️⃣ Increased competition for aquatic food and space 2️⃣ Disruption in migration and reproduction patterns of aquatic fauna 3️⃣ Disruption of aquatic food web 4️⃣ Increase in oxygen production
questions.e: Ocean darkening pushes light-dependent species toward the surface, leading to increased competition for food and space. It disrupts feeding, migration, and reproduction patterns and stresses plankton communities at the base of the food web. Statement IV is incorrect because oxygen production would decrease, not increase; marine phytoplankton produces over 50% of Earth's oxygen and would be negatively impacted by reduced light penetration in the photic zone. This darkening threatens global fisheries and climate regulation .

questions.q: Q.44) The 'Gyan Post' initiative recently seen in the news, aims to:
o: offer free online courses for vocational training
facilitate affordable delivery of non-commercial educational books
promote door-to-door digital literacy through postal workers
create a national registry of book publishers
questions.e: 'Gyan Post' is a dedicated postal service introduced by the Department of Posts for the affordable delivery of educational, cultural, social, and religious books. It aims to support the New Education Policy by making printed materials more accessible in remote and rural areas. Under this scheme, textbooks for various boards, universities, and competitive exams can be sent at lower costs. The initiative is designed to bridge the educational divide across India .

questions.q: Q.45) Which of the following statements is/are correct with reference to the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB)? 1️⃣ It is an attached office under the Ministry of Home Affairs. 2️⃣ It was set up to fulfil the obligations under the Convention on International Civil Aviation, 1944. 3️⃣ It has unrestricted access to all relevant evidence from any agency without seeking prior consent from any government authorities.
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect because the AAIB is an attached office of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, not Home Affairs. Statement II is correct; it was established to fulfill state obligations under the 1944 Chicago Convention. Statement III is also correct; to ensure independence and efficiency, the AAIB has immediate, unrestricted access to all evidence from any organization without needing prior consent from government or judicial authorities. Its work is governed by the Aircraft Act of 1934 and specific investigation rules updated in 2017 and 2021 .

questions.q: Q.46) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Surinsar-Mansar Wildlife Sanctuary: Hosts Dal lake 2️⃣ Kali Tiger Reserve: Part of Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary 3️⃣ Idukki Wildlife Sanctuary: Located on banks of Periyar river 4️⃣ Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve: Largest Tiger reserve in India
questions.e: Only the middle two pairs are correctly matched. Kali Tiger Reserve in Karnataka includes the Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary and Anshi National Park. Idukki Wildlife Sanctuary in Kerala is located between the Periyar and Cheruthoni Rivers. Statement I is incorrect; while the Surinsar-Mansar sanctuary in Jammu and Kashmir contains its own namesake lakes, Dal Lake is located in Srinagar. Statement IV is incorrect; the Veerangana Durgavati reserve is in Madhya Pradesh, but the largest tiger reserve in India is the Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve in Andhra Pradesh .

questions.q: Q.47) With reference to zero-coupon bonds, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They pay periodic interest. 2️⃣ They are redeemed at full face value upon maturity. 3️⃣ They are purchased at a discounted price.
questions.e: Zero-coupon bonds, also known as discount bonds, do not pay periodic interest (statement I is incorrect). They are purchased at a deep discount, significantly below their face value. Upon maturity, the investor is redeemed at the full face value, and the difference between the initial discounted purchase price and that final value represents the interest earned over the bond's life. These are often long-term instruments used for long-range financial goals .

questions.q: Q.48) Consider the following pairs with reference to the colour-coded alerts issued by International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL): 1️⃣ Silver Notice: Identification and tracing of criminal assets 2️⃣ Yellow Notice: Locate missing person 3️⃣ Black Notice: Warn about a person who is considered a possible threat to public safety
questions.e: Only the first two pairs are correctly matched. A Silver Notice is used to identify and trace criminal assets; India recently secured its first-ever Silver Notice via the CBI. A Yellow Notice helps locate missing persons, often minors. Statement III is incorrect; a Black Notice is used to seek information on unidentified bodies, not public threats. A Green Notice is the one used to warn about individuals considered a potential threat to public safety. These notices are issued by the General Secretariat at a member country's request .

questions.q: Q.49) With reference to UNESCO Creative Cities Network (UCCN), which one of the following is an odd one out?
o: Jaipur: Creative City of Crafts and Folk Arts
questions.e: Srinagar is the odd one out because it was designated a Creative City of Crafts and Folk Arts in 2021, not Gastronomy. Hyderabad is the only Indian city currently holding the Gastronomy designation, though Lucknow was recently nominated for it. Other Indian cities in the network include Jaipur (Crafts and Folk Arts, 2015), Varanasi, Chennai, and Gwalior (all for Music), and Kozhikode (Literature, 2023). The UCCN was launched in 2004 to foster collaboration among cities that recognize creativity as a strategic factor for sustainable development .

questions.q: Q.50) The Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Report 2024 is published by which one of the following organizations?
questions.e: The GEM Report is an annual, independent report published by UNESCO. It is the primary authoritative reference used to monitor progress toward SDG 4, which aims for inclusive and equitable quality education. The 2024 theme is "Leadership in Education". According to latest estimates, the global out-of-school population has risen to 272 million. This includes approximately 78 million primary-age children and 130 million upper secondary-age youth .

questions.q: Q.51) With reference to SCORES Portal, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is launched by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). 2️⃣ It aims to address investor grievances against market infrastructure institutions.
questions.e: SCORES (SEBI Complaint Redressal System) is a centralized web-based platform launched by SEBI in 2011. It facilitates the redressal of investor grievances against listed companies, registered intermediaries, or market infrastructure institutions. A newer version, SCORES 2.0, was launched on April 1, 2024, which reduced the maximum resolution time for complaints from 30 days to 21 calendar days. Complaints are automatically routed to the relevant regulated entity for resolution .

questions.q: Q.52) Recently, the Centre issued 'Model Rules for Felling of Trees in Agricultural Lands'. In this context, which of the following are the likely objectives behind promoting agroforestry in India? 1️⃣ Enhancing tree cover outside traditional forest areas 2️⃣ Reducing dependence on timber imports 3️⃣ Supporting India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement
questions.e: All three are objectives of the new model rules. The Centre aims to promote agroforestry to double farmers' incomes, increase tree cover outside forests, and mitigate climate change. By simplifying felling and transit rules, the government hopes to reduce timber imports and ensure sustainable land use. This support aligns with India's climate goals and NDCs under the Paris Agreement. Applicants must register their plantations on the National Timber Management System (NTMS) portal and provide geotagged images for monitoring .

questions.q: Q.53) The recently launched Samarth Incubation Program primarily aims to:
o: provide vocational training to underprivileged youth in rural areas
support startups in the next generation telecom and IT sectors
enhance agricultural productivity through AI-based solutions
promote rural entrepreneurship through promoting traditional crafts
questions.e: The Samarth Incubation Program, launched by the Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DoT), supports startups creating next-generation technologies in telecom software, 5G/6G, cybersecurity, AI, and Quantum technologies. The program aims to help startups bridge the gap from ideation to commercialization by providing access to C-DoT lab facilities, expert mentorship, and furnished office space for six months. Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is the implementation partner for this initiative. It targets DPIIT-recognized startups with sustainable and scalable business models .

questions.q: Q.54) Consider the following statements with reference to Valley fever: 1️⃣ It is a fungal infection that affects lungs. 2️⃣ It is classified as Neglected Tropical Disease (NTD). 3️⃣ It is most common in the winter season. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only Statement I is correct: Valley fever (coccidioidomycosis) is a lung infection caused by the soil-dwelling fungus Coccidioides. Statement II is incorrect because it is not classified as an NTD; it is primarily found in the southwestern US, parts of Mexico, and Central and South America. Statement III is incorrect because the infection is most common in late summer and fall, peaking between September and November, often during periods of significant dust and dirt. Symptoms include cough, fever, and fatigue, and it can be misdiagnosed as bacterial pneumonia .

questions.q: Q.55) 'Portulaca Bharat', recently discovered in the Aravalli Hills, is a new species of which of the following?
questions.e: Portulaca bharat is a new species of flowering plant discovered in the rocky, semi-arid landscape of the Aravalli Hills near Jaipur. It is a succulent plant with pale-yellow flowers and thick roots, uniquely adapted to extreme environments. This species is an Indian endemic and has been provisionally assessed as "data deficient" by the IUCN. The genus Portulaca includes about 153 species globally, known for their toughness and water-storing tissues. Its discovery highlights the hidden biodiversity of the Aravalli region .

questions.q: Q.56) The Order of Makarios III Grand Cross' was recently awarded to the Prime Minister of India by which one of the following countries?
questions.e: The Grand Cross of the Order of Makarios III is a prestigious honor in Cyprus, named after the country's first president. It was awarded to the Indian Prime Minister during a visit in 2025, the first by an Indian PM in over 20 years. The order, established in 1991, recognizes outstanding leadership and contributions that positively impact Cyprus or the international community. It is one of several recent global honors received by the PM, alongside awards from Russia, Bhutan, and the US .

questions.q: Q.57) Consider the following statements with reference to India's Extended Trajectory-Long Duration Hypersonic Cruise Missile (ET-LDHCM): 1️⃣ It is completely indigenous defence technology. 2️⃣ It is capable of achieving maximum speeds up to Mach 8. 3️⃣ It can be launched from land, air and naval platforms.
questions.e: The ET-LDHCM is an indigenous technology developed by DRDO under the classified Project Vishnu. It can achieve top speeds of Mach 8 (approx. 11,000 km/h) and has a range of about 1,500 km, allowing for strikes deep into enemy territory. It is highly flexible and can be launched from land, aircraft, or naval platforms. Designed for both conventional and nuclear missions, it flies at low altitudes and can make mid-course corrections, making it difficult to intercept. This development places India among an elite group of countries with hypersonic weapons .

questions.q: Q.58) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Lac insects secrete laccaic acid, which is utilized in the production of natural lac dye. 2️⃣ Palash tree serves as a primary host tree for lac insects. 3️⃣ India is currently the world's leading producer of lac.
questions.e: Lac insects feed on host trees like the Palash (Butea monosperma) and secrete shellac resin and laccaic acid. Laccaic acid is used to produce a red dye for food coloring, textiles, and folk art. India is the world's leading producer and exporter of lac, with production centered in states like Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh. Recent research suggests the lac pigment may actually be produced by a symbiotic yeast-like organism living inside the insect, which supplies the necessary tyrosine that the insect cannot produce .

questions.q: Q.59) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Mount Lewotobi Laki-laki: Indonesia 2️⃣ Mount Merapi: Japan 3️⃣ Mount Sinabung: United States of America
questions.e: Only the first pair is correctly matched. Mount Lewotobi Laki-laki is a twin volcano located in Indonesia's East Nusa Tenggara province. Mount Merapi is also an active stratovolcano in Indonesia, located on the island of Java, not Japan. Mount Sinabung is also located in Indonesia (Karo, North Sumatra), not the USA. Indonesia is situated along the "Ring of Fire," a seismically active string of volcanoes around the Pacific Ocean where 75% of Earth's active volcanoes and 90% of earthquakes occur .

questions.q: Q.60) "Two individuals, often referred to as Alice and Bob, are exchanging secure information using particles whose physical states collapse if observed. When a third party tries to intercept the exchange, the system detects the intrusion instantly due to the disturbance in particle states". The above method of communication is best described as:
questions.e: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) uses quantum entanglement to create unbreakable communication security. If an eavesdropper ("Eve") tries to intercept the encryption key, the physical state of the quantum particles (photons) is disturbed, immediately alerting "Alice" and "Bob" and shutting down the process. This makes data effectively unhackable. ISRO recently demonstrated entanglement-based QKD over 300 meters, and DRDO/IIT Delhi successfully tested free-space QKD over a distance of more than 1 km. The state of entangled particles remains linked regardless of distance .

questions.q: Q.61) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Operation Sindhu: Rescue Indian nationals stranded in conflict-hit Iran 2️⃣ Operation Kaveri: Repatriate Indian citizens were stranded in Sudan 3️⃣ Operation Ganga: Rescue Indian citizens stranded in Ukraine
questions.e: All three pairs are correctly matched. Operation Sindhu was launched to rescue Indian students from Iran during the 2025 Israel-Iran War. Operation Kaveri was the 2023 mission to evacuate thousands of citizens from conflict-hit Sudan using both aircraft and naval ships. Operation Ganga was the mission to rescue Indians, primarily students, from Ukraine during the war with Russia in 2022. Another mission, Operation Brahma, was launched in 2025 to provide humanitarian aid and search and rescue following a devastating earthquake in Myanmar .

questions.q: Q.62) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ World Investment Report: World Bank 2️⃣ Global Drought Outlook Report: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development 3️⃣ Global Economic Prospects Report: International Monetary Fund 4️⃣ Tracking SDG 7: The Energy Progress Report: International Solar Alliance
questions.e: Only Pair II is correct. The Global Drought Outlook report is indeed published by the OECD and assesses drought management strategies. Statement I is wrong because the World Investment Report is by UNCTAD. Statement III is wrong because Global Economic Prospects is published by the World Bank. Statement IV is wrong because Tracking SDG 7 is a joint report by five agencies including the IEA, World Bank, and WHO, not solely the ISA. India's economy is projected to grow at a steady rate of 6.7% through FY27 according to the latest World Bank data .

questions.q: Q.63) With reference to the PM-Wi-Fi Access Network Interface (WANI) Scheme, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It allows local businesses like kirana stores and tea stalls to set up Wi-Fi hotspots without requiring any license. 2️⃣ There is no cap on tariffs charged to Public Data Offices (PDOs).
questions.e: Statement I is correct: local businesses like kirana stores can become Public Data Offices (PDOs) and set up hotspots without needing a license or fee from the DoT. Statement II is incorrect; TRAI has prescribed a cap on tariffs charged to PDOs to keep public Wi-Fi affordable. Specifically, service providers must offer retail FTTH plans to PDOs at a tariff not exceeding twice the rate applicable to regular retail subscribers. The scheme uses a network of Public Data Office Aggregators (PDOAs) to manage authorization and accounting for these hotspots .

questions.q: Q.64) Consider the following statements with reference to the FASTag: 1️⃣ It uses Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology for automatic toll collection at plazas. 2️⃣ It is solely managed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
questions.e: FASTag uses RFID technology to communicate with scanners at toll plazas for automatic payments. Statement II is incorrect because it is managed by both the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and the NHAI. While made mandatory nationwide in 2021, it was first launched as a pilot in 2014. An optional annual pass now allows private, non-commercial vehicles toll-free travel for 200 trips per year, though this pass only works at NHAI-operated plazas and not on private or state-run expressways .

questions.q: Q.65) With reference to United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is mandated under the Istanbul Declaration on Human Settlements. 2️⃣ It was formed under the resolution 25/206 of the UN. 3️⃣ The UN-Habitat Assembly convenes every four years.
questions.e: UN-Habitat is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote sustainable urbanization, with its mandate shaped by the Vancouver and Istanbul Declarations. It was formally established in 2002 under resolution 56/206 (referred to here as 25/206) as a subsidiary organ of the General Assembly. In 2018, its governance structure was updated to include the UN-Habitat Assembly, which represents all 193 member states and meets every four years. It is the UN's focal point for human settlement matters .

questions.q: Q.66) Consider the following Union Territories (UTs) of India: 1️⃣ Delhi 2️⃣ Ladakh 3️⃣ Jammu and Kashmir 4️⃣ Lakshadweep 5️⃣ Puducherry The President can make regulations for peace, progress and good governance for how many of the above UTs?
questions.e: Under Article 240, the President can make regulations for Lakshadweep, Puducherry (only when its legislature is suspended), and Ladakh (added via the 2019 Reorganisation Act). The President can also regulate the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Daman and Diu. Delhi and Jammu and Kashmir have special status or legislative assemblies and are not covered under Article 240 for these regulations. Thus, only three of the listed UTs are covered .

questions.q: Q.67) Consider the following statements with regard to Census exercise in India: 1️⃣ The administrative boundaries of districts, tehsils, villages and towns are frozen before every Census. 2️⃣ The census data must be released within one year of its conclusion. 3️⃣ The Registrar General of India, the nodal agency for conducting the census, functions under the Prime Minister's Office.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; administrative boundaries must be frozen three months before the census begins to ensure accuracy during enumeration. Statement II is incorrect; there is no statutory mandate to release data within a specific timeframe, and it often happens in phases. Statement III is incorrect; the Registrar General of India functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs, not the PMO. The Census is conducted under the Census Act of 1948. Data collection for the next census is set to begin early in 2026 .

questions.q: Q.68) Consider the following statements: Statement I: India is the world's largest emitter of sulfur oxides. Statement II: More than 40% of India's electricity is produced from coal based thermal plants. Statement III: The calorific value of Indian coal is lower than that of the imported coal used in the Thermal Power Plants.
o: Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
questions.e: Statement I is correct; in 2022, India contributed over 20% of global SO2 emissions. Statement II is correct as coal-based thermal plants provide about 50.5% of India's installed capacity. Statement III is correct; Indian coal has half the calorific value of imported coal. Both Statements II and III explain Statement I: India's heavy reliance on coal (II) and the need to burn twice as much Indian coal due to low calorific value (III) results in high SO2 emissions, despite the coal's relatively low sulfur content .

questions.q: Q.69) Consider the following statements with regard to the 'Greater Flamingos': 1️⃣ They fly along the Central Asian Flyway (CAF). 2️⃣ They act as ecosystem engineers for wetlands by improving the productivity and nutrient flow. 3️⃣ They are categorized as 'Endangered' on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.
questions.e: Greater Flamingos are the state bird of Gujarat and migrate along the Central Asian Flyway. They are "ecosystem engineers" because their "pit-foraging" method of feeding creates depressions that improve nutrient flow and wetland productivity. Statement III is incorrect; they are categorized as 'Least Concern' on the IUCN Red List, not endangered. They are a specialized filter-feeding species typically found in saline, alkaline wetlands and are protected under Schedule II of India's Wildlife Protection Act. A new sanctuary for them was recently notified at Dhanushkodi .

questions.q: Q.70) Fusarium graminearum, a pathogen that was recently seen in the news, is a:
questions.e: Fusarium graminearum is a harmful fungus that infects cereal crops like wheat, barley, and corn, particularly in warm, humid conditions. It causes diseases like head blight and produces toxins such as deoxynivalenol, which can cause vomiting and liver damage in humans and livestock. It enters plants through natural openings like stomata and spreads systemically. Recently, two individuals were charged in the US for allegedly smuggling this dangerous biological pathogen for research .

questions.q: Q.71) Consider the following statements with regard to offshore mining in India: 1️⃣ Royalties from mining offshore mineral resources are entirely assigned to the Central Government. 2️⃣ Private sector mining of any mineral in the offshore regions is prohibited.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; Article 297 of the Constitution vests all minerals in India's territorial waters and exclusive economic zone (EEZ) in the Union, so all royalties go to the Central Government. Statement II is incorrect because the 2023 amendment to the Offshore Areas Minerals Act now permits private sector involvement in offshore mining. India's EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles. Recently, there have been protests in Kerala regarding the Union's decision to allow private sector sand mining in offshore regions .

questions.q: Q.72) Which of the following countries are members of the Eurasian Economic Union (EEU)? 1️⃣ Kyrgyzstan 2️⃣ Kazakhstan 3️⃣ Turkmenistan 4️⃣ Uzbekistan
questions.e: The Eurasian Economic Union (EEU) consists of five member states: Russia, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan, and Kazakhstan. Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan are not members. Established in 2015, the union aims for economic integration by allowing the free movement of goods, capital, and labor among its members, similar to the European Union's common market model. India and the EEU are currently entering negotiations for a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) .

questions.q: Q.73) What are quasi satellites?
o: Satellites placed in the orbit of other planets, but maintain communication with the Earth
Asteroids which have the propensity to fall into the Earth's atmosphere in the near future
A satellite that orbits the Sun while remaining under the gravitational influence of a planet
questions.e: A quasi-satellite is typically an asteroid that orbits the Sun but stays close enough to a planet to remain under its gravitational influence. Unlike the Moon (a true satellite), which is primarily bound by the planet's gravity, quasi-satellites are mainly controlled by the Sun's gravity. From the planet, their path appears to loop around it, often in a "peanut" shape. Examples include the asteroid Kamo'oalewa, which China's Tianwen-2 mission aims to sample, and Asteroid Cardea .

questions.q: Q.74) Consider the following statements with reference to First Person View (FPV) Drones: Statement I: FPV drones are often preceded by reconnaissance drones to first identify and locate targets. Statement II: FPV drones have short range and also lack autonomous navigation systems.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Statement I is correct because FPV drones are often used for precision attacks after longer-range reconnaissance drones identify targets. Statement II is also correct; FPV drones typically have a short range and lack autonomous systems, relying instead on a pilot's real-time manual navigation via a live video feed from an onboard camera. Statement II explains Statement I because the drones' technical limitations (short range/lack of autonomy) necessitate the initial identification of targets by other reconnaissance assets before deployment .

questions.q: Q.75) This macaque is known for unique human-like hairstyles, where its tuft of hair forms a cap-like shape with a defined partition. It also eats soils from termite nests to counter digestive issues. This is the most likely description of:
questions.e: The Bonnet macaque (Macaca radiata) is endemic to southern India and is easily identified by a central tuft of hair that forms a "bonnet" with a distinct partition. They are diurnal and adept at swimming. Notably, they eat soil from termite nests (termitaria) to help manage digestive issues, as these soils are rich in minerals like kaolin, similar to ingredients in some human anti-diarrheal remedies. They are currently categorized as 'Vulnerable' by the IUCN. The Kerala government recently sought permission to begin a sterilization program for them .

questions.q: Q.76) Which of the following countries share land borders with Paraguay? 1️⃣ Argentina 2️⃣ Uruguay 3️⃣ Brazil 4️⃣ Bolivia 5️⃣ Chile
o: II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III and IV only
questions.e: Paraguay is a landlocked South American country bordering Argentina (south/southwest), Brazil (east/northeast), and Bolivia (north/northwest). Uruguay is separated from Paraguay by parts of Argentina, and Chile does not share a border with it. The country is divided into two regions by the Paraguay River. Natural boundaries include the Paraná, Pilcomayo, and Apa rivers. The name Paraguay comes from a Guaraní word meaning "river that gives birth to the sea" .

questions.q: Q.77) Which one of the following is called "A gift from Lord Buddha to the people of Sravasti"?
questions.e: Kalanamak rice, grown in the Terai region of Uttar Pradesh, is traditionally known as "Buddha rice". Legend says Lord Buddha gifted this aromatic rice variety with a black husk to the people of Sravasti after his enlightenment. It has been awarded a Geographical Indication (GI) tag and is naturally resilient to drought and diseases like bacterial blight. Its cultivation costs and water usage are significantly lower than basmati rice. The government is pushing for exports of this rice to Buddhist countries .

questions.q: Q.78) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Tral Wildlife Sanctuary: Himachal Pradesh 2️⃣ Amrabad Tiger Reserve: Andhra Pradesh 3️⃣ Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary: Odisha 4️⃣ Indravati National Park: Chhattisgarh
questions.e: Only the fourth pair is correctly matched. Indravati National Park is located in Chhattisgarh and part of the Godavari River basin. Tral Wildlife Sanctuary is in Jammu & Kashmir, providing habitat for the endangered Hangul. Amrabad Tiger Reserve is in Telangana (Nallamala Hills), not Andhra Pradesh. Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary is in Andhra Pradesh and contains India's second-largest mangrove forest. Indravati is noted for having minimal human intrusion despite being in a Naxalite-affected area .

questions.q: Q.79) The acronym MPOWER which is often discussed in the news relates to which of the following:
questions.e: MPOWER is a World Health Organization (WHO) toolkit launched in 2008 to reduce tobacco demand. The acronym stands for Monitor tobacco use, Protect people from smoke, Offer help to quit, Warn about dangers, Enforce advertising bans, and Raise taxes on tobacco. Other WHO toolkits include SHAKE (salt reduction), REPLACE (eliminating trans fats), and SAFE (eliminating trachoma). The 2025 theme for World No Tobacco Day focused on exposing industry tactics used to attract youth to nicotine products .

questions.q: Q.80) Consider the following statements with reference to the Mount Etna: 1️⃣ It is located in the Mediterranean Sea. 2️⃣ It has been recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
questions.e: Mount Etna is Europe's largest and most active volcano, located on the eastern coast of Sicily in the Mediterranean Sea. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013 due to its 500,000-year history of volcanic activity and its importance to geological research. Documented records of its eruptions span over 2,700 years. A significant eruption in 2025 generated renewed scientific interest, with experts debating whether the vertical expulsion of ash resembled a Strombolian or Plinian eruption .

questions.q: Q.81) In which one of the following groups of countries are all members of the G7 grouping?
o: France, Germany, Japan and United Kingdom
Japan, United States, Australia and Italy
United Kingdom, Canada, South Korea and Germany
questions.e: The G7 is an informal group of seven advanced democracies: Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States. India, Australia, and South Korea are not members, although India's PM recently attended a meeting in Canada as an observer. The grouping was originally formed between 1975 and 1976 to coordinate global economic policy. It addresses a range of transnational issues through annual coordination among these seven leading economies .

questions.q: Q.82) Consider the following statements with regard to NAKSHA: 1️⃣ It aims at achieving land records modernisation for the rural areas. 2️⃣ It includes both aerial and field mapping for the surveying.
questions.e: NAKSHA (National geospatial Knowledge-based land Survey of urban Habitations) is a pilot program for modernizing urban land records, not rural ones (statement I is incorrect). Rural land modernization is handled by programs like SVAMITVA. Statement II is correct as NAKSHA uses advanced aerial techniques like LiDAR and 2D Nadir cameras along with field surveys to create a GIS-integrated 3D database. It is being implemented in 157 Urban Local Bodies across India. SVAMITVA, meanwhile, uses drone-based surveys to provide legal property cards to rural residents .

questions.q: Q.83) Out of the 28 States of the Union of India, how many share an international border with Bangladesh?
questions.e: Five Indian states share an international land border with Bangladesh: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. This boundary spans over 4,000 km, making it India's longest international border. West Bengal shares the longest portion at approximately 2,217 km. Tripura’s border is particularly dense, surrounding the state on three sides for about 856 km. Assam shares 263 km, Meghalaya 443 km, and Mizoram 318 km. The border is vital for trade but sensitive due to illegal migration and smuggling issues .

questions.q: Q.84) With reference to Shangri La Dialogue, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an annual Heads of the States summit for deliberation of security issues in the Indo-Pacific. 2️⃣ It is organized by the World Economic Forum (WEF).
questions.e: Both statements are incorrect. The Shangri La Dialogue is a symposium for security experts and stakeholders, not a formal summit, and Heads of State may or may not attend. It is organized by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) and Singapore's Ministry of Defence, not the WEF. Established in 2002, it covers both traditional and non-traditional security threats in the Asia-Pacific region. India's Chief of Defence Staff made statements at the 2025 edition regarding Operation Sindoor .

questions.q: Q.85) The 'Zangezur Corridor', often mentioned in news, aims to connect which one of the following?
o: Georgia to Azerbaijan via the Black Sea maritime route
Azerbaijan's mainland to its Nakhchivan exclave through Armenian territory
Russia to Iran via the Caspian Sea
Turkey to Central Asia bypassing Iran
questions.e: The Zangezur Corridor is a proposed route to connect Azerbaijan's mainland with its Nakhchivan exclave by passing through Armenia's Syunik Province. Historically disputed since WWI, the corridor would link Azerbaijan's transport networks directly to Turkey (Anatolia) and onward to Europe. It is strategically significant for regional connectivity across Eurasia, joining Turkish, Russian, Iranian, and Armenian territories. The project aims to reduce transportation costs and significantly cut travel time between the two Azerbaijani regions .

questions.q: Q.86) Which one of the following statements best describes the atmospheric phenomenon of 'omega block' which was recently seen in the news?
o: Intensive rainfall over a region within a short span of time
Circulatory movement of winds around a low pressure area giving rise to thunderstorms in the region
A high pressure area surrounded by low pressure areas at the same latitude
Precipitation caused by the advective evapotranspiration over land
questions.e: An 'omega block' is a phenomenon where high-pressure air is trapped between two low-pressure areas, forming an upside-down U shape like the Greek letter omega. This configuration blocks the normal movement of weather fronts, leading to prolonged dry conditions under the high pressure and heavy rainfall or storms under the low-pressure areas. These blocks can last for several days, resulting in persistent heatwaves or flooding in the affected regions. They can also increase wildfire risk due to the extended dry periods .

questions.q: Q.87) Consider the following statements with regard to Great Indian Bustard: 1️⃣ It is the heaviest of all the known flying birds. 2️⃣ It is a slow breeder and typically lays only one egg per breeding season.
questions.e: The Great Indian Bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps) is the world's heaviest flying bird and is listed as 'Critically Endangered' by the IUCN. It is a slow breeder, usually laying only one egg per season, which contributes to its declining population. These birds are opportunistic eaters and prefer open, arid grasslands for foraging and nesting, though these habitats are increasingly lost to infrastructure and development. During the breeding season, males use a gular pouch to produce a booming call to attract females .

questions.q: Q.88) It is an aromatic plant that grows well in rainfed regions of the temperate zone. In India, Jammu and Kashmir is the largest cultivator of this plant. It is included in the Purple Revolution, which is aimed at increasing the income of farmers through aromatic crops. The plant is:
questions.e: Lavender is the central crop of the "Purple Revolution" (or Lavender Revolution) launched in 2016 in Jammu and Kashmir. It is a hardy, temperate plant that can tolerate frost and drought. The CSIR-IIIM developed the RRL-12 variety specifically for India's climate. This mission aims to replace traditional crops like maize with high-value lavender to increase farmer incomes and support startups. Rosemary is also aromatic but Jasmine prefers tropical climates, while Lemongrass is mainly grown in tropical regions like the Western Ghats .

questions.q: Q.89) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Khichan Wetland: Gujarat 2️⃣ Menar Wetland Complex: Rajasthan 3️⃣ Wadhvana Wetland: Maharashtra 4️⃣ Sultanpur National Park: Haryana
questions.e: Only the second and fourth pairs are correct. Menar Wetland Complex is in Rajasthan and hosts endangered vultures. Sultanpur National Park is a Ramsar site in Haryana supporting over 220 bird species. Statement I is wrong because Khichan Wetland is in Rajasthan, known for wintering Demoiselle Cranes. Statement III is wrong because Wadhvana Wetland is in Gujarat, not Maharashtra. Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance identified by nine specific criteria like biodiversity or support for waterbirds .

questions.q: Q.90) Which one of the following best describes the practice of 'Aid washing'?
o: Providing funds to international agencies in order to avoid the levy of sanctions by them
Providing military assistance to the warring countries to provide impetus to domestic defense manufacturing industries
Providing humanitarian aid so as to avoid any responsibility for the underlying causes of the recipient's sufferings
Providing financial assistance to a country while ignoring the consequences of that aid
questions.e: 'Aid washing' occurs when political issues are portrayed primarily as humanitarian crises to avoid addressing underlying political and legal responsibilities. By focusing on providing aid, leaders avoid dealing with the root causes of the suffering, which can perpetuate a cycle of dependency. The current situation in Gaza is cited as a prime example, where framing the issue through a lens of humanitarian need allows world leaders to sidestep political responsibility for the civilian suffering. This practice prioritizes short-term aid over solving long-term political drivers .

questions.q: Q.91) With reference to the cultivation of onion in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is grown in the kharif season only. 2️⃣ Loamy alluvial soil is the most preferred soil for the growth of this crop. 3️⃣ Maharashtra is ranked first in terms of onion production.
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect; onions are grown in both Kharif and Rabi seasons, with Rabi accounting for 70% of production. Statements II and III are correct. Deep, friable loamy alluvial soils with good drainage are best for onion cultivation. Maharashtra is the leading producer with a 40% share, followed by Madhya Pradesh at 17%. India is the world's second-largest onion producer and largest consumer. Lasalgaon in Maharashtra is Asia's largest wholesale market for the crop .

questions.q: Q.92) Which one of the following was India's first research station in the Arctic Region?
questions.e: Himadri is India's first Arctic research station, inaugurated in 2008 at Svalbard, Norway. Managed by the NCAOR, it provides field and lab facilities about 1,200 km from the North Pole. Statement A, B, and C (Dakshin Gangotri, Bharati, Maitri) are Indian stations in Antarctica, not the Arctic. The Arctic is strategically important for its massive undiscovered gas, mineral reserves, and rare earth elements. It also plays a vital role in regulating the Earth's climate and influencing Indian monsoon patterns .

questions.q: Q.93) With reference to the Kulsi river, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a tributary of Brahmaputra. 2️⃣ It originates from the Khasi hills of Meghalaya. 3️⃣ It is a natural habitat of the Gangetic Dolphin.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Kulsi is a 220 km long south-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra that joins it in Assam. It is formed by the confluence of the Khri, Krishniya, and Umsiri rivers, which originate in the West Khasi Hills of Meghalaya. It is well-known as a natural habitat for the South Asian River Dolphin (Gangetic Dolphin). Recently, the governments of Assam and Meghalaya decided to jointly set up a 55MW hydro power project on this river .

questions.q: Q.94) 'Bow Echo' phenomenon, recently seen in the news, relates to which one of the following?
questions.e: A Bow Echo is a specific radar pattern representing a curved line of thunderstorms that resembles an archer's bow. It is formed when rain-cooled air sinks to the ground and spreads horizontally, lifting warm air and creating new thunderstorms along the leading edge. These systems typically span 20-100 km and can last up to 6 hours. Inflow from the rear eventually bends the line into its characteristic bow shape. An intense storm that hit Delhi in May was identified as a series of bow echoes on radar .

questions.q: Q.95) Consider the following statements with regard to Personality Rights in India: 1️⃣ These have been explicitly recognized under the Right to Privacy as defined by the Supreme Court. 2️⃣ These include the Right to Publicity, preventing the use of the person's attributes to be commercially used by any other entity. 3️⃣ These can be protected and recognized via the Copyrights Act, 1951 as well as the Indian Patents Act, 1970.
questions.e: Statement II is correct: Personality rights include the Right of Publicity, which allows individuals to limit the commercial use of their likeness, voice, or attributes. Statement I is incorrect; while these rights are loosely traced to privacy, the Supreme Court's Puttaswamy judgment stopped short of explicitly recognizing them. Statement III is incorrect; no specific Indian law, including the Copyright Act of 1957 (not 1951) or Patents Act of 1970, recognizes personality rights per se. The Patents Act even excludes human life from its protections .

questions.q: Q.96) Tardigrades, also known as water bears, are mostly known for:
o: their large scale applicability in genetic research
being indicator organisms for water pollution
their ability to survive in extreme environments
being vectors for the strain of corona virus responsible for recent surge
questions.e: Tardigrades are microscopic invertebrates famous for their extreme resilience, surviving near-absolute zero temperatures, high pressure, vacuum, and intense radiation. They can enter a "tun" state, suspending their metabolism for survival. Because of this, they are used for life sciences experiments in space. Indian astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla will undertake an experiment to study their revival and reproduction on the ISS. They have endured all five mass extinctions on Earth and are believed to produce a fluorescent layer for UV protection .

questions.q: Q.97) Consider the following statements regarding G57 Maximum Ordinance Penetrator (MOP) weapon: 1️⃣ It is a specialized weapon to attack deeply buried enemy facilities. 2️⃣ The warhead in this weapon system is encased in a hardened stainless steel case.
