questions.e: The G57 MOP is a GPS-guided "bunker buster" designed to strike hard, deeply buried targets. Its warhead is encased in a special high-performance steel alloy case, allowing it to maintain its integrity during impact while carrying a large explosive payload. Statement II is correct; this hardened casing is essential for its earth-penetrating function. Israel recently used this US-made weapon to target underground nuclear facilities in Iran. It is one of the most specialized earth-penetrating strike weapons in modern arsenals .

questions.q: Q.98) 'Stratospheric Aerosol Injection (SAI)', a geoengineering technique proposed to limit the warming of Earth, is aimed at mimicking or simulating which one of the following natural phenomena?
o: Volcanic eruptions releasing certain particles into the atmosphere
Filtration of solar radiations by the Ozone layer
Mineralization of carbon dioxide by the carbon cycle
Auroras caused by powerful solar flares
questions.e: SAI aims to mimic the natural cooling effect observed after explosive volcanic eruptions, which release particles into the stratosphere that scatter sunlight back into space. By continuously injecting sulfur dioxide into the lower stratosphere, sunlight-reflecting sulfate aerosols would be formed. This is a form of Solar Radiation Management (SRM) designed to reflect solar rays before they reach Earth. SAI is proposed as a climate intervention to rapidly mitigate the harmful effects of global warming, acting like a synthetic volcanic eruption .

questions.q: Q.99) Consider the following statements with regard to Counter Terrorism Committee: 1️⃣ It was established under the UNSC 1267 resolution. 2️⃣ It consists of both permanent and non-permanent members of the United Nations Security Council. 3️⃣ It can impose sanctions on any individual or group suspected of committing terrorist activities.
questions.e: Statement II is correct; the CTC is composed of all 15 members of the UNSC, including both permanent and non-permanent ones. Statement I is incorrect; it was established under Resolution 1373 after the 9/11 attacks, not 1267. Statement III is incorrect; the CTC has no mandate to impose sanctions or designate terrorists; that authority belongs to other bodies like the 1267 Sanctions Committee. The CTC’s role is technical and compliance-based, helping states implement counter-terrorism obligations. Pakistan recently attained the Vice Chair of this committee .

questions.q: Q.100) Which of the following are the benefits associated with use of Nano Urea in agriculture? 1️⃣ It is produced through an energy-efficient and environmentally friendly process with reduced carbon emissions. 2️⃣ It leads to higher nutrient use efficiency due to better crop absorption. 3️⃣ It enhances crop productivity while enhancing soil and water quality. 4️⃣ It completely eliminates the need for conventional urea application.
questions.e: Nano Urea is produced through an energy-efficient process with reduced carbon footprints and provides nutrient availability of over 80%, far higher than conventional urea. Its foliar application enhances crop productivity by about 8% and benefits soil, air, and water quality. Statement IV is incorrect because it complements but does not entirely replace the need for conventional urea in all cases. IFFCO Nano Urea liquid was the first such fertilizer notified by the Government of India. IFFCO is now setting up its first overseas plant in Brazil .

questions.q: Q.1) With regard to the National Green Hydrogen Mission, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It aims to develop 5 million metric tonnes of green hydrogen production capacity per annum by 2030. 2️⃣ It provides financial incentives for domestic manufacturing of electrolysers. 3️⃣ India's first indigenously-built green hydrogen plant was commissioned at Kandla Port.
questions.e: The National Green Hydrogen Mission, approved in 2022, aims to make India a leading producer. By 2030, it envisions a production capacity of at least 5 million metric tonnes per annum. Under the SIGHT programme, the mission provides financial incentives for domestic electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production. India's first Make-in-India green hydrogen plant in the port sector was commissioned at Kandla, Gujarat .

questions.q: Q.2) 'Kodali Karuppur' and 'Kovai Kora' are the types of:
questions.e: Kodali Karuppur and Kovai Kora are traditional handloom sarees. The Kodali Karuppur silk saree was patronized by the Thanjavur Maratha kings and combines hand painting, block printing, and brocade weaving. The Kovai Kora cotton saree, which holds a GI tag, is a blend of silk and cotton pioneered by the Devanga community in Sirumugai .

questions.q: Q.3) With reference to Cable Internet and Satellite Internet, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Unlike Cable Internet, Satellite Internet offers internet access regardless of location. 2️⃣ Unlike Cable Internet, Satellite Internet offers lower latency.
questions.e: Satellite internet provides access regardless of location because signals are beamed from satellites and can be received anywhere with a clear sky view, unlike cable which requires physical infrastructure. However, satellite internet has higher latency than cable because signals must travel a longer distance between Earth and space, causing slight delays .

questions.q: Q.4) Which one of the following microorganisms is used to degrade Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET), the plastic most commonly used in bottles and food packaging?
questions.e: Ideonella sakaiensis, discovered near a Japanese plastic recycling facility, can completely degrade Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET). The bacterium breaks PET into environmentally safe building blocks that can then be metabolized. Scientists are exploring such microbial degradation as a sustainable solution to plastic pollution .

questions.q: Q.5) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Indian clouds are more polluted than those in countries like China, Pakistan, Italy, and the USA. 2️⃣ Eastern Himalayas experience higher polluted clouds containing toxic metals from vehicular and industrial emissions over foothill regions.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect because Indian clouds remain less polluted than those in China, Pakistan, Italy, and the USA. Statement II is correct as a study found clouds over the Eastern Himalayas transport toxic metals like Cd, Cr, Cu, and Zn originating from vehicular and industrial emissions in foothill regions .

questions.q: Q.6) In the context of public finance, what is "short transfer"?
o: Diversion of receipts meant for the Consolidated Fund into the Contingency Fund of India
Non-release of States' tax devolution share as per Finance Commission recommendations
Failure to transfer the full amount of cess collected to the designated reserve funds
Transfer of surcharge proceeds directly to State governments without Parliamentary approval
questions.e: A "short transfer" occurs when the full amount of a cess or levy collected is not transferred from the Consolidated Fund of India (CFI) to the designated Reserve Funds in the Public Account of India. The CAG highlighted a short transfer of 3.69 lakh crore of cess proceeds as of March 2024 .

questions.q: Q.7) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Sumatran rhino — Smallest of all living rhino species 2️⃣ Javan rhino — Only Asian rhino with two horns 3️⃣ Indian rhino — Most threatened of all rhino species 4️⃣ African rhino — Largest of all rhino species
questions.e: Only two pairs are correct. Pair I is correct; Sumatran rhinos are the smallest. Pair II is incorrect; the Sumatran rhino (not Javan) is the only Asian species with two horns. Pair III is incorrect; the Javan rhino (not Indian) is the most threatened. Pair IV is correct; White rhinos (African) are the largest .

questions.q: Q.8) With regard to the Stem Cells, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Undifferentiated cells can give rise to heart muscle cells and blood cells. 2️⃣ Differentiated cells can be reprogrammed back into the state of pluripotency. 3️⃣ Pluripotent cells cannot be cultured in the lab.
questions.e: Statements I and II are correct. Undifferentiated pluripotent stem cells can give rise to all differentiated cells in the body, including heart and blood cells. Differentiated cells like skin cells can be reprogrammed back to pluripotency by expressing specific master regulator genes. Statement III is incorrect as scientists are now capable of capturing and culturing pluripotent cells .

questions.q: Q.9) It is located on the banks of the river Chandrabhaga, built by a ruler of the Hoysala dynasty, and classified as a focal point of the Warkari pilgrimage. Which is this temple?
questions.e: The Vitthal Rukmini Temple in Pandharpur stands on the banks of the Chandrabhaga River. It was originally built by King Vishnuvardhana of the Hoysala Empire (1108–1152 CE). It is the principal center of worship for Vitthal and the focal point of the Warkari pilgrimage during Aashadhi and Kartiki Ekadashi .

questions.q: Q.10) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Tropical rainfall can sometimes reduce vertical mixing in the upper layers of the ocean. 2️⃣ Cold pools during tropical rain cool the ocean's surface and increase the transfer of heat from the water to the air.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: Both statements are correct, and II explains I. Heavy tropical rain is often accompanied by "cold pools" of dry air that cool the ocean surface and pull heat out effectively. This makes the surface water heavier and more stable, which reduces vertical mixing rather than promoting it .

questions.q: Q.11) Which one of the following shows the unique characteristic of remaining intact throughout the winter months despite the subzero temperature?
questions.e: Sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.) can withstand extreme temperatures from -43°C to +40°C and is drought resistant. Its berries are highly nutritious, containing higher concentrations of Vitamin C than amla or oranges. It has been used for centuries in the traditional 'Amchi' medicine system of Ladakh .

questions.q: Q.12) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Senegal 2️⃣ Mauritania 3️⃣ Mali 4️⃣ Niger. How many of the above countries are part of the Sahel region?
questions.e: The Sahel is a semiarid transitional zone between the Sahara Desert and the humid savannas, running through Senegal, Mauritania, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. It covers 12 countries in total and is home to 400 million people. All four listed countries are part of this region .

questions.q: Q.13) Consider the following statements with regard to the Leap-1 Mission: 1️⃣ It is India's first commercial space mission. 2️⃣ It is a collaborative initiative of India and France. 3️⃣ It is proposed to be launched on the indigenously developed P30 satellite platform.
questions.e: Statements I and III are correct. LEAP-1 is India's first commercial space mission, led by the startup Dhruva Space. It utilizes the indigenously developed P-30 satellite platform. Statement II is incorrect; it is an Indo-Australian collaboration (not French) scheduled for launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9 .

questions.q: Q.14) The world is experiencing a fourth mass coral bleaching event. In the above context, which one of the following is a prerequisite to make a final determination of a mass bleaching event?
o: It must be reported in both tropical and temperate seas.
It must affect at least half of the world's coral reefs.
It must last for a minimum of two consecutive years.
It must be confirmed in each of the the major ocean basins.
questions.e: A mass coral bleaching event is officially confirmed only when bleaching is observed in all major ocean basins. The current fourth global event was confirmed by NOAA and ICRI as bleaching spread across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans starting in early 2023 .

questions.q: Q.15) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is the largest of the surviving lemur species. 2️⃣ It is endemic to the island of Madagascar. 3️⃣ It is mainly arboreal in nature. Which is this species?
questions.e: The Indri (Indri indri) is the largest lemur in the world and is endemic to Madagascar, specifically the eastern tropical rainforests. While they spend much of their lives in trees, they are not strictly arboreal. They are currently classified as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List .

questions.q: Q.16) Which of the following are classified as creamy layer in India? 1️⃣ Children of parents who hold constitutional posts 2️⃣ Children of parents employed in Group A services of the Union or All India Services 3️⃣ Children of parents whose gross annual income is more than 8 lakh, including income from agricultural land
questions.e: Points I and II are correct. Children of constitutional functionaries and Group A/Class I officers are excluded from OBC reservation. Point III is incorrect because while the income limit is ₹8 lakh (since 2017), income from salary and agricultural land is excluded from this calculation .

questions.q: Q.17) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Improve water retention capacity of soils 2️⃣ Adsorb CO2 from industrial exhaust gases 3️⃣ Increase heat resistance of buildings 4️⃣ Treatment of wastewater. How many of the above are the potential benefits of biochar?
questions.e: Biochar offers all four benefits. In agriculture, it improves water retention and soil health. Modified biochar can adsorb CO2 from industrial exhausts. In construction, it can increase building heat resistance by 20%. It is also effective for low-cost wastewater treatment .

questions.q: Q.18) The Hyblaea puera Nucleopolyhedrosis Virus (HpNPV)' was recently seen in the media in the context of which one of the following?
o: It prevents massive defoliation in teak crops.
It increases the water retention capacity of the crops.
It decreases the drought resistant capacity of the crops.
It promotes faster growth of crops in semi arid regions.
questions.e: HpNPV causes a lethal infection in teak defoliator larvae, preventing massive defoliation of teak trees. It is entirely host-specific, targeting only the teak defoliator, making it safe for the forest ecosystem. This eco-friendly technology has significant export potential for teak-cultivating countries .

questions.q: Q.19) Consider the following statements with regard to the Great Barrier Reef: 1️⃣ It contains the world's largest collection of coral reefs. 2️⃣ It is located on the south-west coast of Australia. 3️⃣ It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
questions.e: Statements I and III are correct. The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef collection and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981. Statement II is incorrect; it is located off the north-east coast of Australia (Queensland) in the Coral Sea .

questions.q: Q.20) Consider the following statements with regard to Hepatitis D: 1️⃣ It only affects people who already have Hepatitis B. 2️⃣ It has been classified as cancerous by the World Health Organisation (WHO).
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Hepatitis D is an "incompetent" virus that requires Hepatitis B for replication, meaning it only affects those already infected with HBV. The WHO recently reclassified Hepatitis D as cancerous, noting its co-infection with HBV significantly increases liver cancer risk .

questions.q: Q.21) What is Ectopic Pregnancy?
o: A pregnancy in which the foetus exhibits an abnormal growth in the uterus
A pregnancy in which triplets are born prematurely
A pregnancy in which the fertilised egg implants itself outside the uterus
A pregnancy in which assisted reproductive technologies are involved
questions.e: An ectopic pregnancy occurs when a fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, most commonly in the fallopian tube (tubal pregnancy). Because only the uterus is designed to carry a growing embryo, these pregnancies cannot proceed normally and can be life-threatening due to bleeding .

questions.q: Q.22) The Dardanelles strait connects which of the following water bodies?
o: Aegean Sea and Sea of Marmara
questions.e: The Dardanelles is a narrow strait in Turkey connecting the Aegean Sea and the Sea of Marmara. It separates the continent of Europe from Asia Minor. Together with the Bosporus (which connects the Sea of Marmara to the Black Sea), it provides the only sea connection for Black Sea lands to the world .

questions.q: Q.23) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Biligiri Rangaswamy Temple Tiger Reserve — Agasthyamala 2️⃣ Bandipur Tiger Reserve — Nilgiri 3️⃣ Mudumalai Wildlife Sanctuary — Seshachalam
questions.e: Only Pair II is correctly matched. Bandipur Tiger Reserve is an essential component of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Pair I is incorrect; Biligiri Rangaswamy Temple Tiger Reserve is in Karnataka, while Agasthyamala is in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Pair III is incorrect; Mudumalai is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (not Seshachalam) .

questions.q: Q.24) 'Dhirio', a traditional form of bull fighting, is practised in which one of the following states of India?
questions.e: Dhirio is a traditional form of bullfighting in Goa, dating back to the Portuguese era. Unlike Spanish bullfighting, it involves two bulls fighting each other in paddy fields without killing the animal. It was banned in 1996 under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, though legislators recently sought its legalization .

questions.q: Q.25) The Equator Prize, also known as the Nobel Prize for Biodiversity Conservation, is awarded by which one of the following organisations?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
questions.e: The Equator Prize is organized by the Equator Initiative within the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It recognizes outstanding community efforts to reduce poverty through biodiversity conservation. India's Bibi Fatima Women's SHG was a recent winner under the theme of women and youth leadership for climate action .

questions.q: Q.26) Consider the following statements with regard to the State Health Regulatory Excellence Index (SHRESTH): 1️⃣ It will categorise the States and the Union Territories as 'manufacturing states' and 'primarily distribution states/UTs' for ranking purposes. 2️⃣ It will be implemented by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO).
questions.e: Both statements are correct. SHRESTH is a national initiative proposed by the CDSCO to benchmark and strengthen state drug regulatory systems. It ranks entities by dividing them into 'manufacturing states' and 'primarily distribution states/UTs' based on specific indices like infrastructure and licensing .

questions.q: Q.27) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Cash payments 2️⃣ Bank transfers 3️⃣ Standing orders 4️⃣ UPI AutoPay 5️⃣ Cheque payments. How many of the above are 'pull transactions'?
questions.e: Only two are pull transactions: UPI AutoPay and Cheque payments. Pull payments are controlled by the payee, who withdraws funds based on prior authorization. Cash payments, bank transfers, and standing orders are 'push payments' where the payer initiates and controls the transaction .

questions.q: Q.28) With reference to the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is declared by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). 2️⃣ The theme for 2025 is 'Indigenous Peoples and Artificial Intelligence - Defending Rights, Shaping the Future'.
questions.e: Statement II is correct as the 2025 theme focuses on Indigenous Peoples and AI. Statement I is incorrect because the day (August 9) was decided by the UN General Assembly (UNGA), not UNESCO, to mark the first meeting of the UN Working Group on Indigenous Populations .

questions.q: Q.29) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Sawalkote — Beas 2️⃣ Tato II — Siyom 3️⃣ Seli — Chenab 4️⃣ Miar — Satluj
questions.e: Only two pairs are correct. Pair II is correct; Tato II is on the Siyom River in Arunachal Pradesh. Pair III is correct; Seli is in the Chenab Basin. Pair I is incorrect; Sawalkote is on the Chenab (not Beas). Pair IV is incorrect; Miyar is on the Chenab (not Satluj) .

questions.q: Q.30) Consider the following statements with regard to the Semicon India Programme: 1️⃣ It extends a fiscal support of 100% of the project cost for setting up of Silicon CMOS based Semiconductor Fabs in India. 2️⃣ It provides a Product Design Linked Incentive of up to 50% of the eligible expenditure subject to a ceiling of ₹15 crore per application. 3️⃣ It is implemented under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM).
questions.e: Statements II and III are correct. The programme provides a Design Linked Incentive (DLI) of up to 50% (ceiling ₹15 crore) and is implemented by the ISM. Statement I is incorrect because the fiscal support for Silicon CMOS Semiconductor Fabs is 50% of the project cost, not 100% .

questions.q: Q.31) Consider the following statements with regard to the symbiotic relationship in Lichens: 1️⃣ It involves a mycobiont and one or more photobionts. 2️⃣ It helps build soil and serves as nature's bioindicator.
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Lichens are a symbiosis between a fungus (mycobiont) and a photosynthetic partner (photobiont), such as green alga or cyanobacteria. They play vital roles in building soil, feeding insects, and acting as sensitive bioindicators of ecosystem health .

questions.q: Q.32) It is a radioactive isotope of hydrogen. It is produced naturally from interactions of cosmic rays with gases in the upper atmosphere, and is also a by-product of nuclear reactors. When combined with phosphor, it creates glow-in-the-dark lighting such as exit signs, emergency lighting in buildings and airport runway lights. It is:
questions.e: Tritium is a radioactive isotope of hydrogen with two neutrons. It occurs naturally from cosmic rays and is a byproduct of nuclear reactors. It is used for glow-in-the-dark lighting and as a tracer in biomedical research for diseases like cancer and AIDS .

questions.q: Q.33) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ MERITE — Improve governance of technical education 2️⃣ Bharat Forecast System — Predict small-scale weather features accurately 3️⃣ CATCH Grant Program — AI solutions to strengthen cancer screening
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. MERITE improves the quality and governance of technical education. The Bharat Forecast System uses high resolution to predict small-scale weather features. The CATCH Grant Program supports AI solutions for cancer screening and diagnostics .

questions.q: Q.34) The 'Notch signaling pathway' in animals is primarily involved in:
questions.e: The Notch signaling pathway is a highly conserved mechanism essential for proper embryonic development in all animals. It facilitates communication between adjacent cells to regulate cell development. Recent AI research has even designed proteins to activate this pathway to boost T-cell production .

questions.q: Q.35) Which of the following countries are the members of the BIMSTEC? 1️⃣ Thailand 2️⃣ Vietnam 3️⃣ Myanmar 4️⃣ Malaysia
questions.e: Thailand and Myanmar are members of BIMSTEC. The seven-member grouping also includes Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, and Sri Lanka. Vietnam and Malaysia are not members of BIMSTEC. The organization was established in 1997 through the Bangkok Declaration .

questions.q: Q.36) 'Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of Artificial Intelligence (FREE-AI)' in the financial sector has been established by:
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
questions.e: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) established a committee in 2023 to develop the FREE-AI framework for the financial sector. The framework is built on pillars like infrastructure, policy, and protection to ensure AI adoption remains ethical, responsible, and transparent in finance .

questions.q: Q.37) Recently, the Government of India has made certain regulations mandatory for the manufacturing of wind turbines in the country. Which of the following are included in it? 1️⃣ Sourcing of 100% wind turbine components from domestic suppliers 2️⃣ Storing of all wind turbine data within India 3️⃣ Setting up of Research & Development centres by all manufacturers in India within one year 4️⃣ Certification of wind turbines by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)
questions.e: Regulations II, III, and IV are mandatory. Turbine data must be stored in India, R&D centers must be set up within a year, and BIS certification is required. Regulation I is incorrect; the mandate requires key components (65–70% of cost), not 100% of all components, to be from domestic suppliers .

questions.q: Q.38) With regard to the toll charges on National Highways in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Perpetual tolling allows toll collection to continue even after project costs are recovered. 2️⃣ Toll rates are revised annually through a fixed increment and partial linkage with the Wholesale Price Index.
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Perpetual tolling allows collection to continue after project costs are recovered, credited to the Consolidated Fund of India. Toll rates are revised annually using a 3% fixed increment and partial Wholesale Price Index (WPI) adjustment .

questions.q: Q.39) Which of the following islands are part of the 'Polynesian Triangle'? 1️⃣ Hawaii 2️⃣ Bermuda 3️⃣ New Zealand 4️⃣ Azores 5️⃣ Easter
o: I, II, III, IV and V
questions.e: The Polynesian Triangle is defined by three corners: Hawaii, New Zealand, and Easter Island. Bermuda and the Azores are located in the Atlantic Ocean and are not part of the Pacific territory of Polynesia .

questions.q: Q.40) Orbiting Carbon Observatories (OCO) Program, a series of dedicated Earth remote sensing satellites that were designed specifically to observe atmospheric CO2 from space, is an initiative of:
questions.e: The Orbiting Carbon Observatory (OCO) program is an initiative of NASA. OCO-2, launched in 2014, was NASA's first dedicated satellite to study atmospheric CO2 variability and quantify sources and sinks on regional scales .

questions.q: Q.41) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Adaptation to local agro-climatic conditions 2️⃣ High climate resilience 3️⃣ Yield stability under low-input systems 4️⃣ Pest and disease tolerance 5️⃣ Conservation of on-farm genetic diversity. How many of the above are ecological benefits of landraces (locally adapted crop varieties)?
questions.e: Landraces provide all five ecological benefits. They are adapted to local conditions, reducing the need for external fertilizers. They show high climate resilience and yield stability in low-input systems. They often possess natural pest tolerance and preserve vital genetic diversity .

questions.q: Q.42) Consider the following statements with regard to the Alpine Musk Deer and Himalayan Musk Deer: 1️⃣ Both are endemic to Western Himalayas. 2️⃣ Both are listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List. 3️⃣ Both are herbivores.
questions.e: Statements II and III are correct. Both species are listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List due to overexploitation and both are ruminant herbivores. Statement I is incorrect; the Himalayan musk deer occurs across Nepal, Bhutan, India, Pakistan, and China (not just Western Himalayas) .

questions.q: Q.43) Consider the following statements with regard to the Special Rupee Vostro Account (SRVA): 1️⃣ It enables foreign entities to settle transactions in Indian Rupees (INR) with Indian banks. 2️⃣ Authorised Dealer (AD) needs prior approval from the Reserve Bank of India to open SRVAs for their overseas correspondent banks.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; SRVA allows foreign entities to settle trade in INR, supporting the rupee's internationalization. Statement II is incorrect because the RBI recently removed the requirement for AD banks to seek prior approval to open SRVAs for overseas correspondent banks .

questions.q: Q.44) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Registered Unrecognized Political Parties cannot avail the benefits of income tax exemption. 2️⃣ Only Recognised Political Parties can appoint their star campaigners. 3️⃣ If a party does not contest elections continuously for six years, it is taken off the list of registered parties.
questions.e: Statement III is correct; parties that do not contest elections for six continuous years are delisted. Statement I is incorrect because all registered parties can avail income tax exemptions. Statement II is incorrect as RUPPs can appoint up to 20 star campaigners (recognised parties can appoint 40) .

questions.q: Q.45) Consider the following protected areas: 1️⃣ Gir National Park 2️⃣ Desert National Park 3️⃣ Mitiyala Wildlife Sanctuary 4️⃣ Barda Wildlife Sanctuary. How many of the above are known to host Asiatic Lions?
questions.e: Only three of these host Asiatic Lions. Gir National Park is their primary home. Mitiyala and Barda also host lion populations. Desert National Park (Rajasthan) does not host Asiatic Lions. The total population rose to 891 by 2025 .

questions.q: Q.46) Which of the following statements are correct with regard to the fisheries sector in India? 1️⃣ India is the world leader in shrimp production. 2️⃣ The inland fisheries contribute more than 50% of the country's total fish production. 3️⃣ The PM Matsya Sampada Yojana aims to improve aquaculture productivity, and doubling fisheries exports to 1 lakh crores.
questions.e: All three statements are correct. India leads the world in shrimp production. Inland fisheries now contribute about 70% of total production. PMMSY targets increasing productivity to 5 tonnes/Ha and doubling exports to ₹1 lakh crore .

questions.q: Q.47) Which one of the following missions is described by the ISRO as a chance to test out life-support systems, to observe how crew members work and respond in a Mars-like setting without ever leaving Earth?
questions.e: Human Outer Planetary Exploration (HOPE) is ISRO's first high-altitude analogue mission, conducted in the Mars-like terrain of Ladakh's Tso Kar valley. It serves as a rehearsal for future human spaceflight, testing life-support systems and crew responses in isolation .

questions.q: Q.48) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ PM e-DRIVE — Promotion of electric mobility — Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 2️⃣ PM UJJWALA — Make clean cooking fuel available to households — Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 3️⃣ PM JUGA — Socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes — Ministry of Education
questions.e: Only two rows are correctly matched. Row II is correct. Row I is incorrect because PM e-DRIVE is implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industry. Row III is incorrect as PM JUGA is coordinated by 17 ministries, primarily the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (not just Education) .

questions.q: Q.49) Which one of the following best describes the term Amphibious Warfare?
o: A joint operation by two friendly countries
A joint domain of conventional and nuclear warfares
Ajoint domain of cyberspace and conventional warfares
A joint operation by navy, ground and air forces of a country
questions.e: Amphibious warfare is a complex joint operation where naval units, supported by air forces, transport a land force to a hostile shore to establish a beachhead. It requires seamless integration of all three services. Historical examples include the D-Day landings .

questions.q: Q.50) The recently released General-Purpose AI (GPAI) Code of Practice is an initiative of:
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
questions.e: The GPAI Code of Practice is an initiative of the European Commission to help the tech industry comply with the EU AI Act's legal obligations regarding safety and transparency. Over twenty major tech companies, including Google and Microsoft, have committed to this voluntary tool .

questions.q: Q.51) Consider the following statements about e-Sushrut: 1️⃣ It is a cloud-based Hospital Management Information System (HMIS). 2️⃣ It has been developed by the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR). 3️⃣ As of now, it connects only government healthcare facilities.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; e-Sushrut is a cloud-based HMIS. Statement II is incorrect as it was developed by the NHA and C-DAC (not CSIR). Statement III is incorrect because it is designed for private outpatient clinics and small hospitals, not just government facilities .

questions.q: Q.52) With reference to Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojna, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an Employment Linked Incentive Scheme only for the manufacturing sector. 2️⃣ It aims to support the creation of over 3.5 crore jobs within a two-year period. 3️⃣ It provides an incentive of up to Rs 30,000 per month per new employee to employers for creation of new job opportunities.
questions.e: Statement II is correct as the scheme aims to create 4 crore total jobs (including 2.59 crore for employers). Statement I is incorrect; it covers all sectors, though it has a special focus on manufacturing. Statement III is incorrect because the employer incentive is up to ₹3,000 per month, not ₹30,000 .

questions.q: Q.53) Consider the following statements about National Gopal Ratna Awards: 1️⃣ These awards recognize and encourage excellence in the livestock and dairy sector. 2️⃣ They aim to promote and conserve indigenous cattle and buffalo breeds. 3️⃣ These are given on the occasion of National Milk Day on 26th November every year.
questions.e: All three statements are correct. The awards recognize excellence in the dairy sector , specifically targeting the conservation of indigenous breeds. They are presented annually by the DAHD on National Milk Day, November 26 .

questions.q: Q.54) What is "Golden Dome", recently in the news?
o: It is the U.S-Israel joint program to enhance the Iron Dome system for protection against short-range rockets.
It is a space-based missile defense shield to neutralize enemy's Inter-Continental Ballistic Missiles (ICBMs).
It is a NATO-led project to create a space-based radar system for monitoring global satellite movements.
It is an Indian cyber-defense program designed to shield critical infrastructure from digital attacks.
questions.e: The Golden Dome is a proposed U.S. defense initiative for a multi-layered shield using space-based sensors and lasers to intercept ICBMs and hypersonic weapons in their boost phase. It has been compared to the Strategic Defense Initiative of the 1980s .

questions.q: Q.55) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Tonga — Polynesian island nation 2️⃣ Great Chagos Bank — World's largest atoll structure 3️⃣ Jeju Island — Volcanic island in Japan 4️⃣ Spratly Islands — Disputed islands in South China Sea 5️⃣ Sulawesi — Island in Indonesian archipelago
questions.e: Only four pairs are correct. Pair III is incorrect because Jeju is a volcanic island in South Korea, not Japan. The others are correct: Tonga is in Polynesia , Great Chagos Bank is the largest atoll , Spratlys are disputed , and Sulawesi is Indonesian .

questions.q: Q.56) Green Ammonia is produced by the combination of:
questions.e: Green Ammonia is produced by combining green hydrogen (from water electrolysis using renewable energy) with atmospheric nitrogen via Haber-Bosch synthesis. Unlike "grey" ammonia, this process is carbon-free. It is used in fertilizers, synthetic fibers, and as a shipping fuel .

questions.q: Q.57) With regard to Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis (PAM), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a rare infection of the brain caused by the amoeba Naegleria fowleri. 2️⃣ It spreads through ingestion of contaminated food.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; PAM is caused by the "brain-eating amoeba" Naegleria fowleri and has a 97% fatality rate. Statement II is incorrect as the amoeba enters through the nose (not ingestion) and travels the olfactory nerve to the brain .

questions.q: Q.58) Consider the following statements with regard to Almond cultivation: 1️⃣ It is mainly cultivated in the tropical and coastal regions of India. 2️⃣ It grows well in deep, well-drained loamy soils with average rainfall of 75 to 110 cm.
questions.e: Statement II is correct; almonds thrive in loamy, well-drained soils with 75–110 cm of rainfall. Statement I is incorrect because almonds require a colder climate (7°C–24°C) and are grown in hilly regions like J&K and Himachal Pradesh, not tropical coasts .

questions.q: Q.59) With reference to Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ All listed companies in India must ensure at least 25% public shareholders. 2️⃣ Companies with market capital above 1,00,000 crore are required to offer to the public at least 5% of the post issue market capital.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; SEBI mandates a minimum 25% public shareholding for all listed companies to ensure liquidity. Statement II is incorrect as companies with market caps between ₹1–5 lakh crore must offer at least ₹6,250 crore and 2.75% of post-issue capital, not 5% .

questions.q: Q.60) Which one of the following South Asian countries recently eliminated Rubella?
questions.e: The WHO recently verified that Nepal has eliminated rubella. It is the sixth country in the South-East Asia region to achieve this, joining Bhutan, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Timor-Leste, and North Korea. Rubella is a contagious viral infection that can cause severe birth defects if contracted by pregnant women .

questions.q: Q.61) Consider the following statements with regard to the Sakura Science Programme: 1️⃣ It is a student exchange program offered by the Government of Japan. 2️⃣ It provides result-based financial grants to researchers in emerging sectors. 3️⃣ India is not part of the program.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; it is a Japanese initiative (JST) allowing young learners to explore science and culture. Statement III is incorrect as India joined in 2016. Statement II is incorrect because it is an exchange program for students and does not provide research grants .

questions.q: Q.62) With regard to the e-Jagriti Portal of the Government of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Law and Justice. 2️⃣ It enables consumers to file complaints, track case status and access judgments online.
questions.e: Statement II is correct as e-Jagriti provides consumers online access to file complaints and track cases. Statement I is incorrect because the initiative belongs to the Department of Consumer Affairs under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, not the Law Ministry .

questions.q: Q.63) Which of the following statements is/are correct with regard to the Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)? 1️⃣ It can be manufactured from 'used cooking oil'. 2️⃣ The Government of India has mandated a 10% SAF blending in conventional jet fuel by 2027. 3️⃣ Its usage can reduce greenhouse gas emissions by up to 80% depending on feedstock.
questions.e: Statements I and III are correct. SAF can be made from used cooking oil and renewable feedstocks and can reduce emissions by up to 80%. Statement II is incorrect; the initial mandate for 2027 is 1% blending for international flights, not 10% .

questions.q: Q.64) Which of the following statements is/are correct with regard to the 'Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee', recently seen in the news? 1️⃣ It is an advisory body formed under the aegis of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). 2️⃣ Its primary objective is to develop a legally binding international treaty to end plastic pollution.
questions.e: Statement II is correct; the INC's mandate is to draft a legally binding treaty to end plastic pollution across the lifecycle of plastics. Statement I is incorrect because the INC was formed under the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), not the UNFCCC .

questions.q: Q.65) With reference to the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It was initially founded to address the large-scale displacements caused by the Vietnam War. 2️⃣ It is governed by the UN General Assembly and the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC). 3️⃣ It is the first UN Agency to be awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. 4️⃣ It started the Nansen Refugee Award in 1954 for recognition of outstanding service to the cause of refugees, displaced or stateless people.
questions.e: Statements II, III, and IV are correct. UNHCR is governed by the UNGA and ECOSOC , was the first UN agency to win a Nobel Peace Prize , and started the Nansen Refugee Award in 1954. Statement I is incorrect; it was founded in 1950 following WWII .

questions.q: Q.66) The Kalai-II Hydroelectric Project, recently seen in the news, is being built on which one of the following rivers?
questions.e: The 1,200 MW Kalai-II hydroelectric project is proposed to be built on the Lohit River in the Anjaw district of Arunachal Pradesh. It is being developed by THDC India Limited and recently underwent public hearings for environmental clearance .

questions.q: Q.67) Which of the following statements best describes the term 'Triple Chain of Command', recently seen in the news?
o: It refers to the accountability of Local Self-Governments to the State Governments, which then is accountable to the Union Government.
It is a military doctrine that ensures a clear line of authority from the supreme commander to the ground forces, integrating all three branches of the armed forces.
It is a framework for judicial review, where the judiciary can assess the actions of the executive, legislature, and civil services.
It means the accountability of the civil service to the ministers, the ministers to the legislature, and the legislature to the electorate.
questions.e: The 'triple chain of command' ensures democratic accountability by linking civil servants to ministers, ministers to the legislature, and the legislature to the electorate. The Supreme Court emphasized this concept in 2023 regarding the control an elected government must have over its civil servants .

questions.q: Q.68) With reference to the Government Bond Yield, consider the following: 1️⃣ Upgrade in sovereign credit ratings of India 2️⃣ Rise in public debt 3️⃣ Reduction in the Repo Rate by the Reserve Bank of India 4️⃣ Rise in inflation. Which of the above factors can affect bond yields in the long term?
questions.e: All four factors affect bond yields. Rating upgrades lower yields. Increased debt (fiscal deficit) raises yields due to higher supply. Lower repo rates signal looser policy, typically lowering yields. Rising inflation lowers bond prices and increases yields to compensate for lost purchasing power .

questions.q: Q.69) Which of the following statements is/are correct with regard to the Made in India Label scheme? 1️⃣ It is a voluntary certification scheme to help manufacturers demonstrate that their products are of good quality. 2️⃣ The initiative is being led by the NITI Aayog.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; it is a voluntary certification to brand Indian-made products and guarantee their authenticity. Statement II is incorrect as the initiative is led by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), not NITI Aayog .

questions.q: Q.70) With regard to the Agni-5, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a surface-to-surface ballistic missile with a range of more than 8000 kilometres. 2️⃣ It is capable of carrying a nuclear warhead of about 1.5 tonnes. 3️⃣ It is equipped with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) technology. 4️⃣ It uses a three-stage engine whose upper stage is cryogenic.
questions.e: Statements II and III are correct. Agni-5 carries a 1.5-tonne nuclear warhead and is equipped with MIRV technology for multiple targets. Statement I is incorrect; its range is over 5,000 km, not 8,000 km. Statement IV is incorrect as it uses a solid-fuel propulsion system, not a cryogenic upper stage .

questions.q: Q.71) Consider the following accreditation boards: 1️⃣ National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH) 2️⃣ National Board for Quality Promotion (NBQP) 3️⃣ National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies (NABCB) 4️⃣ National Accreditation Board for Education and Training (NABET) 5️⃣ National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL). How many of the above fall under the purview of the Quality Council of India?
questions.e: All five boards—NABH, NBQP, NABCB, NABET, and NABL—function as executive boards under the Quality Council of India (QCI). The QCI is an autonomous organization established in 1997 to establish a national accreditation structure and lead the quality movement in India .

questions.q: Q.72) Consider the following statements with regard to Euglena: 1️⃣ It exhibits both autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition. 2️⃣ Its overgrowth can lead to hypoxic conditions in lakes and ponds.
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Euglena is a "borderline" organism that photosynthesizes in light (autotrophy) but feeds on organic matter in darkness (heterotrophy). Overgrowth leads to diurnal oxygen fluctuations, resulting in hypoxic conditions at night that are dangerous for aquatic life .

questions.q: Q.73) Exercise Samanvay Shakti, recently seen in the news, is a:
o: naval exercise between India and ASEAN nations focusing on disaster management
military-civil integration exercise by the Indian Army to address regional challenges
joint counter-terrorism exercise by the National Security Guard (NSG) and state police forces.
tri-service military exercise of India with the United States of India
questions.e: Exercise Samanvay Shakti is a military-civil integration exercise led by the Indian Army in Assam and Manipur. It aims to foster synergy between security forces, government departments, and civil institutions to address regional challenges through a unified, coordinated approach .

questions.q: Q.74) Consider the following statements with regard to Charge-Coupled Devices (CCDs): 1️⃣ It converts light into electrical signals using an array of capacitors that transfer charges in sequence. 2️⃣ It is widely used in digital cameras and telescopes for capturing high-quality images.
questions.e: Both statements are correct. A CCD converts photons into electrical charges via the photoelectric effect, storing them in pixels and transferring them sequentially like "buckets of water" to form an image. They are fundamental in digital cameras, medical imaging, and astronomical telescopes .

questions.q: Q.75) With reference to Blue Carbon ecosystem, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is the carbon captured and stored by coastal and marine ecosystems. 2️⃣ It accounts for half of the ocean's carbon absorption. 3️⃣ It stores the majority of their carbon below ground.
questions.e: All three statements are correct. Blue carbon refers to CO2 stored in coastal ecosystems like mangroves and seagrasses. Though covering only 2% of the ocean surface, they provide 50% of its carbon absorption. Unlike terrestrial forests, they store most carbon in long-lived, waterlogged sediments below ground .

questions.q: Q.76) With reference to the Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an autonomous body working under the Ministry of Education. 2️⃣ It funds social science research and provides research-based policy inputs.
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The ICSSR is an autonomous organization under the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education. Established in 1969, its mandate is to promote, fund, and coordinate social science research while providing research-based policy inputs to the government .

questions.q: Q.77) Consider the following statements with regard to the Huntington's Disease: 1️⃣ It is an autoimmune disorder caused by a mutation in the HTT gene. 2️⃣ The presence of the HTT gene in parents always leads to the development of Huntington's Disease in children.
questions.e: Both statements are incorrect. Huntington's is a genetic neurodegenerative disorder, not autoimmune. It follows an autosomal dominant pattern where a child has a 50% chance (not 100% or 75%) of inheriting the mutation from a carrier parent. Patients have urged the government to classify it as a rare disease .

questions.q: Q.78) Consider the following statements with regard to the SMILE scheme: 1️⃣ It is a Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. 2️⃣ It provides comprehensive rehabilitation for transgenders and people engaged in begging. 3️⃣ It includes educational linkages for children of rehabilitated persons.
questions.e: All three statements are correct. SMILE is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. It provides comprehensive rehabilitation, including healthcare and skill development, for transgender persons and those engaged in begging. It also ensures children of rehabilitated individuals are enrolled in schools .

questions.q: Q.79) With regard to the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a global collaboration that develops protocols for mobile telephony, including standards for 5G and 6G technologies. 2️⃣ It works under the aegis of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a specialized agency of the United Nations. 3️⃣ Telecommunications Standards Development Society of India is the organizational partner of 3GPP from India.
questions.e: Statements I and III are correct. 3GPP develops technical specifications for 5G and 6G. TSDSI is India's organizational partner in 3GPP. Statement II is incorrect; while it submits standards to the ITU, 3GPP is an independent consortium and does not work under ITU's aegis .

questions.q: Q.80) Consider the following statements with regard to Sundarbans Tiger Reserve: 1️⃣ It is the largest tiger reserve in India in terms of area. 2️⃣ It is the only mangrove ecosystem in the world to harbour tigers.
questions.e: Statement II is correct; the Sundarbans is the world's only mangrove ecosystem where tigers have adapted to swimming and saline water. Statement I is incorrect; after its 2025 expansion, it is India's second-largest tiger reserve, with Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam remaining the largest .

questions.q: Q.81) Consider the following statements about Vithalbhai Patel: 1️⃣ He was the first Indian to become the President of the Central Legislative Assembly. 2️⃣ He opposed Mahatma Gandhi's decision to suspend the Non-Cooperation Movement. 3️⃣ He along with Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das founded the Swaraj Party in 1923.
questions.e: All three statements are correct. Vithalbhai Patel became the first Indian President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925. He opposed the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement and was a co-founder of the Swaraj Party in 1923. He also issued the Patel-Bose manifesto calling for radical leadership .

questions.q: Q.82) Consider the following statements with regard to the India's BioE3 Policy: 1️⃣ It is an initiative by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to promote a regenerative bioeconomy. 2️⃣ The National Biofoundry Network is an integral part of BioE3 Policy. 3️⃣ It focuses on India's domestic biomanufacturing capabilities for precision biotherapeutics and smart proteins. 4️⃣ The goal of the policy aligns with the vision of 'Net-Zero' carbon economy of the country.
questions.e: Statements II, III, and IV are correct. The policy establishes a National Biofoundry Network , focuses on biotherapeutics and smart proteins , and aligns with 'Net-Zero' goals. Statement I is incorrect; BioE3 is an initiative of the Department of Biotechnology under the Ministry of Science and Technology (not MoEFCC) .

questions.q: Q.83) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Quick Reaction Surface to Air Missiles 2️⃣ Very Short-Range Air Defence System 3️⃣ Laser-based Directed Energy Weapon 4️⃣ MALE Unmanned Aerial Vehicle. How many of the above are components of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System of India?
questions.e: Only the first three are components of the IADWS: QRSAM, VSHORADS, and a high-power laser-based Directed Energy Weapon (DEW). MALE UAV is not a component; rather, the IADWS is designed to neutralize aerial threats like drones and swarm drones .

questions.q: Q.84) Consider the following statements regard to the selenium pollution: 1️⃣ Selenium is a trace element that is beneficial to the human body in small quantities but can become toxic in excess. 2️⃣ There is no known safe level of exposure to selenium. 3️⃣ Copper smelting activity is a source of selenium pollution in India.
questions.e: Statements I and III are correct. Selenium is an essential trace element for metabolism but becomes toxic in excess (selenosis). Copper smelting is a major pollution source as it releases selenium dioxide. Statement II is incorrect; safe permissible limits exist, such as the BIS limit of 0.01 mg/L for drinking water in India .

questions.q: Q.85) 'Aadi Vaani', was recently launched for which one of the following purposes?
o: To establish community radio networks for remote tribal regions
To translate tribal languages through an Artificial-Intelligence-based portal
To sell tribal handicrafts via an online platform
To promote traditional Indian music forms of tribal communities
questions.e: Adi Vaani is an AI-powered translation tool designed to revitalization tribal languages and cultures. It can translate text and speech between Hindi/English and languages like Bhili, Gondi, and Santali. It aims to support digital literacy and preserve folklore .

questions.q: Q.86) With reference to the Anamalai Tiger Reserve, which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: It is a part of Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve.
It is located on the southern side of the Western Ghat landscape in Tamil Nadu.
Synchronous lighting by mega congregations of fireflies is observed here every year.
It hosts the world heritage sites of Kariyan shola and Manjampatti.
questions.e: Statement (c) is incorrect; Anamalai Tiger Reserve is not part of the Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve (which includes Periyar and Kalakkad-Mundanthurai). Other statements are correct: it is in Tamil Nadu , features synchronous firefly bioluminescence , and hosts UNESCO sites like Kariyan shola .

questions.q: Q.87) Consider the following statements with regard to Project 17 Alpha (P17A): 1️⃣ It was launched to build seven advanced stealth frigates for the Indian Navy. 2️⃣ Its ships have been designed in-house by the Indian Navy's Warship Design Bureau (WDB).
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Project 17A builds seven advanced stealth frigates, with INS Udaygiri and INS Himgiri recently commissioned in 2025. These ships are designed in-house by the WDB, demonstrating India's growing self-reliance in naval shipbuilding under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative .

questions.q: Q.88) With regard to New World screwworm, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an insect, native to tropical and subtropical America. 2️⃣ It causes myiasis disease. 3️⃣ Its life cycle is independent of the host. 4️⃣ It has been eradicated from the United States of America.
questions.e: Statements I, II, and IV are correct. This insect (man-eater) is native to America, causes the priority disease myiasis by burrowing into tissue, and was eradicated from the US by 1991. Statement III is incorrect; its life cycle is host-dependent as females must lay eggs on the living tissue of warm-blooded animals .

questions.q: Q.89) With regard to the National Designated Authority (NDA), which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It has been established to implement the Paris Agreement. 2️⃣ It is a 21 member committee headed by the Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; the NDA was established to implement Article 6 of the Paris Agreement for carbon markets. Statement II is incorrect as the 21-member committee is headed by the Secretary of the Environment Ministry, not the Minister .

questions.q: Q.90) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Super Garuda Shield — India and Saudi Arabia 2️⃣ Exercise Maitree — India and Egypt 3️⃣ Exercise BRIGHT STAR — India and Thailand 4️⃣ SLINEX — India and Sri Lanka
questions.e: Only pair IV is correctly matched; SLINEX is a bilateral naval exercise between India and Sri Lanka. Pair I is incorrect; Super Garuda Shield 2025 was between Indonesia and the US. Pair II is incorrect; Maitree is with Thailand. Pair III is incorrect; Bright Star is hosted by Egypt .

questions.q: Q.91) What is the 'Inverted duty structure' in the context of Indian taxation?
o: It arises when the tax rate levied on intermediate inputs and raw materials exceed the tax rate on the final product.
It is the liability to pay tax on the recipient of supply of certain goods or services instead of the supplier of such goods or services.
It is the tax paid on purchases for the business which can be deducted on output tax.
questions.e: An inverted duty structure occurs when the GST rate on raw materials is higher than the rate on the finished product. For example, before 2025, man-made fibers were taxed at 18% while garments were at 5%. The GST Council recently addressed this for textiles and fertilizers .

questions.q: Q.92) With regard to the Rare Earth Magnets (REM), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are stronger than conventional magnets due to their high magnetic energy density. 2️⃣ Neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets are the most common type of rare-earth magnet. 3️⃣ They are brittle and vulnerable to corrosion.
questions.e: All three statements are correct. Rare earth magnets have high magnetic energy density. NdFeB magnets are the most common type. They are brittle and vulnerable to corrosion, often requiring nickel-plating to prevent oxidation. India currently faces a severe shortage of these magnets for EVs .

questions.q: Q.93) With regard to the National Awards to Teachers (NAT), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is given to teachers from School, Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and Polytechnics. 2️⃣ It is conferred by the Ministry of Education. 3️⃣ The parameters of evaluation give maximum weightage to research publications.
questions.e: Statements I and II are correct. Since 2023, NAT includes exemplary faculty from HEIs and Polytechnics. It is conferred by the Ministry of Education. Statement III is incorrect because maximum weightage is given to teaching-learning effectiveness and outreach, not research publications .

questions.q: Q.94) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Tawi River flows through the city of Jammu. 2️⃣ The Sutlej River originates near Manali in Himachal Pradesh. 3️⃣ The Pong Dam is built on the Beas River in Himachal Pradesh. 4️⃣ The Beas River joins the Sutlej River in Punjab.
questions.e: Statements I, III, and IV are correct. The Tawi flows through Jammu. The Pong Dam is on the Beas in Himachal. The Beas joins the Sutlej in Punjab. Statement II is incorrect; the Sutlej originates in Tibet from Lake Rakshastal, not in Himachal Pradesh .

questions.q: Q.95) With regard to the Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) Scheme, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It provides working capital loans to street vendors. 2️⃣ The beneficiaries who repay their second loan can access a UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card and are eligible for digital cashback incentives up to 1,600. 3️⃣ It is jointly implemented by the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs and Department of Financial Services.
questions.e: All three statements are correct. PM SVANidhi provides working capital loans. Successful repayment of the second loan grants access to a UPI-linked RuPay card with ₹1,600 cashback. It is jointly implemented by MoHUA and the DFS .

questions.q: Q.96) With regard to the Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an educational management information system by the Ministry of Women and Child. 2️⃣ It enables recognised schools to record and submit real-time data on school profile, students, and teachers.
questions.e: Statement II is correct; schools submit real-time data on students, teachers, and profiles through three integrated modules. Statement I is incorrect as UDISE+ is under the Ministry of Education (Department of School Education & Literacy), not the Ministry of Women and Child .

questions.q: Q.97) With regard to Gorumara National Park, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is located in the Dooars-Terai of West Bengal and is renowned for riverine grasslands and sal forests. 2️⃣ It has the highest population of one-horned rhinoceros in the country.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; Gorumara is in West Bengal's Jalpaiguri district and features riverine grasslands enriched by the Murti and Raidak rivers. Statement II is incorrect; while it has rhinos, the highest concentration is in Kaziranga National Park in Assam .

questions.q: Q.98) With regard to the Glanders, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a highly contagious disease affecting horses, mules and donkeys. 2️⃣ It is caused by the virus Burkholderia mallei.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; Glanders is a fatal, contagious disease affecting equines with zoonotic potential for humans. Statement II is incorrect as it is caused by a bacterium (Burkholderia mallei), not a virus. It is a notifiable disease under the PCICDA Act .

questions.q: Q.99) What are Salina aurantiamaculata and Salina pseudomontana, recently seen in the news?
questions.e: These are two new species of springtails (Collembola) discovered in West Bengal. Springtails are tiny soil-dwelling arthropods that act as "ecosystem engineers" by breaking down organic matter and recycling nutrients. This was the first Salina discovery in India in over 40 years .

questions.q: Q.100) With regard to the recent study about Gangotri Glacier, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Gangotri Glacier has lost about 10% of its snowmelt flow due to rising temperatures and reduced snowfall. 2️⃣ The reduced winter precipitation is one of the major factors for the change in the regime of the glacier.
questions.e: Both statements are correct. A study confirms Gangotri lost ~10% of snowmelt flow between 1980 and 2020 due to rising temperatures. The glacier's peak discharge shifted from August to July because of reduced winter precipitation and earlier summer melting .

questions.q: Q.1) What is the primary function of Dendritic Nanotubes (DNTs), recently identified in the brain?
questions.e: DNTs are tiny tubes, about 3 micrometers long, that connect dendrites of neighboring neurons. Researchers at Johns Hopkins University confirmed they transfer electrical signals by allowing charged particles like calcium ions to move between neurons. This process can be blocked by inhibiting nanotube formation with cytochalasin D. DNTs also transport molecules like amyloid-beta, suggesting a possible link to Alzheimer’s disease progression.

questions.q: Q.2) With reference to the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, consider the following — 1️⃣ It aims to achieve self-sufficiency in domestic pulses production by 2030-31 2️⃣ It provides for assured maximum procurement of Tur, Urad, and Masoor under the Price Support Scheme
questions.e: The Union Cabinet approved this six-year central scheme with an outlay of ₹11,440 crore to make India self-sufficient in pulses by 2030-31. It targets increasing production to 350 lakh tonnes by expanding cultivation area and improving yields. The mission focuses on tur, urad, and masur, with assured procurement by NAFED and NCCF under the Price Support Scheme (PSS).

questions.q: Q.3) Which of the following missions provides earth observation data useful for monitoring land deformation, biomass, and glaciers? — 1️⃣ ISRO PSLV-C61 2️⃣ Axiom Mission 3️⃣ NISAR Mission
questions.e: NISAR is a joint Earth observation mission between NASA and ISRO using dual-frequency radar for high-resolution imagery. Its objectives include monitoring land deformation (earthquakes, landslides), measuring biomass changes, and tracking glaciers. PSLV-C61 is a launch vehicle mission, not an observation mission. Axiom refers to private astronaut missions to the ISS for scientific research.

questions.q: Q.4) The HKU5 virus is sometimes mentioned in the news with reference to which one of the following diseases?
questions.e: The bat Merbecovirus HKU5 belongs to the same group as Middle East Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV). They share structural similarities and use similar receptors to infect cells. While HKU5 has only been detected in bats, studies warn it has the potential to infect human cells with just one mutation. Current MERS-CoV vaccines show limited effectiveness against HKU5.

questions.q: Q.5) This festival is celebrated for nine days, overlapping with Navratri, and symbolizes the collective spirit of the people of Telangana. Recently, it set two Guinness World Records for the largest floral arrangement and a synchronised dance performance by women. The festival is:
questions.e: Bathukamma, meaning "The Mother Goddess comes to life," is dedicated to Gauri Devi and celebrated in Telangana. In 2025, it achieved record status for the largest floral decoration (7 tonnes of flowers) and a synchronized performance by 1,354 women. During the festival, women stack local exotic flowers in conical arrangements on wide plates.

questions.q: Q.6) With reference to the recently constituted Payments Regulatory Board (PRB), consider the following — 1️⃣ It is a six-member body chaired by the Finance Secretary 2️⃣ It derives its powers from the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 3️⃣ It regulates all electronic and non-electronic payment systems
questions.e: The RBI set up the PRB to replace the Board for Regulation and Supervision of Payment and Settlement Systems (BPSS). It is chaired by the RBI Governor, not the Finance Secretary. It derives legal authority from the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The board regulates all electronic and non-electronic payment systems, including domestic and cross-border transactions.

questions.q: Q.7) Trichloroethylene (TCE), a cause of concern in recent times for its environmental and health impacts, is mainly used as — 1️⃣ A chemical intermediate in the manufacturing of refrigerants 2️⃣ A degreasing solvent in metal industry 3️⃣ A fertilizer additive in agriculture 4️⃣ A spot remover in commercial dry-cleaning
questions.e: TCE is a volatile synthetic chemical used as an intermediate to produce refrigerants and hydrofluorocarbons. It is widely used for degreasing machinery and precision equipment in the metal industry. It is also a spot remover for grease and oil stains in commercial dry cleaning. It is not used as a fertilizer additive. Long-term exposure is linked to Parkinson’s disease.

questions.q: Q.8) The region often referred to as the 'Amazon of the Seas' extends across the tropical waters of — 1️⃣ Philippines 2️⃣ Maldives 3️⃣ Malaysia 4️⃣ Papua New Guinea
questions.e: The Coral Triangle, known as the "Amazon of the Seas," covers 5.7 million sq. km in the western Pacific. It is home to 75% of world coral species. The core countries are Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Solomon Islands, and Timor-Leste. The Maldives is in the Indian Ocean and is not part of this region.

questions.q: Q.9) With reference to the Ig Nobel Prizes, consider the following — 1️⃣ They are awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences 2️⃣ They are awarded once every five years to promote scientific research 3️⃣ They are given in several categories, including Peace and Psychology 4️⃣ In 2025, two Indian scientists received the award in the Engineering Design category
questions.e: Ig Nobel Prizes are satirical awards presented annually by the magazine Annals of Improbable Research in Boston, not the Royal Swedish Academy. Categories often mirror the Nobels but with humorous twists. In 2025, Indian scientists Vikash Kumar and Sarthak Mittal won in Engineering Design for research on how foul-smelling shoes affect shoe rack experiences.

questions.q: Q.10) Recently, there were deaths of children in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan linked to contaminated cough syrup. In this context, Diethylene Glycol is mainly used in cough syrup for which one of the following reasons?
o: It acts as a toxic solvent.
It acts as a strong sedative.
It increases the viscosity of syrups.
It serves as a substitute of glycerin.
questions.e: Diethylene glycol (DEG) is an industrial solvent used in antifreeze and brake fluids. It is sometimes illegally substituted for pharmaceutical-grade glycerin in cough syrups because it is cheaper. When ingested, it is highly toxic and causes acute kidney injury, renal failure, and multi-organ dysfunction. Contaminated syrups have been linked to over 300 child deaths globally since 2022.

questions.q: Q.11) International Social Security Association (ISSA), works under which of the following organizations?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
questions.e: Founded in 1927, the ISSA promotes excellence in social security administration through guidelines and research. It operates under the auspices of the International Labour Organization (ILO). Headquartered in Geneva, it has over 330 member organizations across 158 countries, including India. India received the ISSA Award 2025 for outstanding achievements in providing social security.

questions.q: Q.12) Consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ JF-17 Thunder: USA 2️⃣ Mirage 2000: France 3️⃣ F-22 Raptor: United Kingdom 4️⃣ Shenyang J-35: Japan
questions.e: The Mirage 2000 is a French-made multirole fighter used by the Indian Air Force. The JF-17 Thunder was jointly developed by China and Pakistan. The F-22 Raptor is an American fifth-generation stealth fighter. The Shenyang J-35 is a Chinese stealth multirole combat aircraft. Only Pair II is correctly matched.

questions.q: Q.13) Consider the following statements with regard to the Preventive Detention in India — 1️⃣ The Constitutional protection against preventive detention extends to both citizens and non-citizens 2️⃣ A person detained under preventive detention must be informed of the grounds for such detention as a matter of right
questions.e: Preventive detention under Article 22 involves confining a person to prevent future offenses rather than punishing past acts. Protections apply to both citizens and non-citizens, though Article 22 excludes enemy aliens and those detained under preventive laws from specific clauses. Communicating grounds for detention is mandatory, though facts may be withheld if disclosure is against public interest.

questions.q: Q.14) The highest motorable road in the world was recently built in Ladakh at which one of the following passes?
questions.e: The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) constructed the world’s highest motorable road at Mig La Pass at 19,400 feet. This broke the previous record of 19,024 feet at Umling La. Developed under Project Himank, the Likaru-Mig La-Fukche road is strategically vital due to its proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

questions.q: Q.15) The term 'Supermoon', sometimes mentioned in the news, refers to which one of the following?
o: A full moon that occurs when the Moon is at its farthest point from Earth
A full or new moon that coincides with the Moon's closest approach to Earth
The alignment of the Sun, Earth, and Moon causing a total solar eclipse
A lunar event visible only during equinoxes when the Moon crosses the Earth's equatorial plane
questions.e: A Supermoon occurs when a full or new moon coincides with the Moon’s closest approach to Earth (perigee) in its elliptical orbit. At perigee, the Moon appears up to 14% larger and 30% brighter than at apogee. These events also strengthen gravitational interactions, resulting in perigean spring tides that slightly raise coastal water levels.

questions.q: Q.16) Consider the following statements with regard to the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) — 1️⃣ It sets global standards for sustainable fishing and seafood traceability 2️⃣ Its certification applies to aquaculture fisheries as well as wild-capture fisheries 3️⃣ The Ashtamudi clam fishery in Kerela was the first in India to be awarded the MSC certification
questions.e: The MSC is a non-profit that sets science-based standards for sustainable wild-capture fishing. It does not certify aquaculture; the Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC) handles that sector. MSC uniquely incorporates FAO frameworks for wild-capture fisheries. The Ashtamudi clam fishery in Kerala was India's first to receive this certification.

questions.q: Q.17) With reference to the recently launched Foreign Currency Settlement System, consider the following — 1️⃣ It was established under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 2️⃣ It is operated by the Reserve Bank of India as part of its global settlement framework 3️⃣ It supports settlements only in US dollar, reflecting its dominant role in global trade and finance
questions.e: The FCSS enables local settlement of foreign currency transactions at GIFT IFSC, reducing settlement time from 48 hours to near real-time. It was established under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. It is operated by CCIL IFSC Limited, not directly by the RBI. While it initially supports US dollars, the framework allows for future inclusion of other major currencies.

questions.q: Q.18) A startup valued at over $1 billion and not listed on the stock exchange is known as a:
questions.e: A unicorn is a privately owned startup valued at over $1 billion. Key traits include high growth potential and disruptive technology. Other terms include "Soonicorns" (valued $500M–$1B), "Decacorns" (over $10B), and "Hectocorns" (over $100B). As of 2025, India has 73 unicorns, making it the world's third-largest startup ecosystem.

questions.q: Q.19) With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthan Mahabhiyan Scheme (PM-KUSUM), consider the following — 1️⃣ It aims to provide free or subsidised electricity to farmers through the installation of rooftop solar systems 2️⃣ It targets to add solar capacity of about 34,800 MW by March 2026 3️⃣ Its beneficiaries include only individual farmers and not any group of farmers
questions.e: PM-KUSUM solarizes agricultural pumps and encourages decentralized generation; free rooftop solar for households falls under PM-Surya Ghar. The scheme targets 34,800 MW of solar capacity by March 2026. Beneficiaries include individual farmers, FPOs, Panchayats, and Co-operatives, not just individuals.

questions.q: Q.20) With reference to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), consider the following — 1️⃣ Part XX of the Constitution deals with the composition and functions of the UPSC 2️⃣ It was set up based on the recommendations of the Lee Commission  3️⃣ Its first Indian Chairman after Independence was H. K. Kripalani
questions.e: Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV (not Part XX) deal with the UPSC. The commission was established on October 1, 1926, following Lee Commission recommendations. H.K. Kripalani became the first Indian Chairman after independence, serving from 1947 to 1949. The UPSC marked its centenary year starting October 2025.

questions.q: Q.21) Which of the following features distinguish Tejas Mk1A from the earlier Tejas Mk1 version? — 1️⃣ 4.5 generation aircraft 2️⃣ Advanced electronically scanned array radar 3️⃣ Delta wing design 4️⃣ Integration with Astra missile system
questions.e: Tejas Mk1A is a 4.5-generation fighter, whereas the original Mk1 is 4th-generation. Key upgrades in Mk1A include an AESA radar (initially Israeli EL/M-2052) and compatibility with the indigenous Astra BVR missile. The delta wing design is a common feature in both variants and does not distinguish them.

questions.q: Q.22) With reference to the Crew Escape System (CES), consider the following — 1️⃣ It is an emergency escape system that pulls the crew module with astronauts to a safe distance in case of launch failure 2️⃣ India's Gaganyaan mission will employ a Puller-type Crew Escape System
questions.e: The CES is a safety mechanism to ensure astronaut survival during launch emergencies by propelling the crew module away from a malfunctioning vehicle. India’s Gaganyaan uses a Puller-type CES (using solid motors), a design shared with Saturn V and Soyuz. ISRO validated this using a single-stage test vehicle powered by a Vikas engine.

questions.q: Q.23) Mission Drishti, recently seen in the news, is related to:
o: India's first underground neutrino observatory for studying neutrinos
A deep-space telescope mission jointly developed by ISRO and NASA
World's first multi-sensor Earth Observation (EO) satellite
India's first interplanetary communication satellite for Mars missions
questions.e: Mission Drishti is the world’s first multi-sensor Earth Observation satellite developed by Bengaluru startup GalaxEye. It is India's largest and highest-resolution privately built satellite (1.5-metre resolution). It carries both Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and optical payloads, allowing all-weather imaging for defense, disaster management, and agriculture.

questions.q: Q.24) Consider the following statements with regard to the Nobel Peace Prize — 1️⃣ Self-nomination leads to automatic disqualification 2️⃣ Nominations for the Nobel Peace Prize remain confidential for 50 years after submission 3️⃣ In 2025, it was awarded to Maria Corina Machado for her efforts to promote democracy in Venezuela 4️⃣ It is the only one which is awarded in Sweden among all Nobel Prizes
questions.e: Self-nomination is prohibited, and all nominations are kept secret for 50 years. In 2025, María Corina Machado won for her democratic struggle in Venezuela. All Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm, Sweden, except for the Peace Prize, which is awarded in Oslo, Norway. Statement IV is thus incorrect.

questions.q: Q.25) The Global Antibiotic Resistance Surveillance Report is published by:
o: Global Antibiotic Research and Development Partnership (GARDP)
questions.e: The WHO releases this report under its Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System (GLASS). The 2025 report analyzed 23 million confirmed cases from over 100 countries. AMR causes approximately 1.27 million global deaths annually due to antibiotic misuse in humans and agriculture.

questions.q: Q.26) Consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ Upper Subansiri: Arunachal Pradesh 2️⃣ Kiru: Sikkim 3️⃣ Naying: Assam 4️⃣ Etalin: Arunachal Pradesh
questions.e: Upper Subansiri (1,800 MW) and Etalin (3,097 MW) are both in Arunachal Pradesh. Kiru is a run-of-the-river project on the Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir, not Sikkim. Naying (1,000 MW) is located on the Siyom River in Arunachal Pradesh, not Assam. Only pairs I and IV are correct.
