questions.q: Q.27) Consider the following statements with regard to International Blue Flag Certification — 1️⃣ It is awarded only to beaches located within marine protected areas 2️⃣ It is accorded by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) 3️⃣ Shrivardhan and Nagaon beaches in Maharashtra received the certification in 2025
questions.e: Blue Flag is awarded by the Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE) in Denmark, not UNEP. It is not limited to marine protected areas; it covers beaches and marinas meeting 33 criteria. In October 2025, five Maharashtra beaches, including Shrivardhan and Nagaon, received this certification.

questions.q: Q.28) Consider the following statements with regard to the Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY) — 1️⃣ It consolidates existing agricultural schemes including PM-KISAN and Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 2️⃣ It aims to transform 100 low-performing agricultural districts across India 3️⃣ At local level, it is operated by the District Dhan Dhaanya Samitis led by District Collectors
questions.e: PMDDKY integrates 36 schemes across 11 ministries, including PM-KISAN and RKVY. Modeled after the Aspirational Districts Programme, it targets 100 underperforming agricultural districts. Local implementation is managed by District Dhan Dhaanya Samitis led by collectors, with monthly monitoring of 117 Key Performance Indicators.

questions.q: Q.29) Which one of the following separates the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat from Pakistan's Sindh Province?
questions.e: Sir Creek, originally 'Ban Ganga,' is a 96-km estuary marking the boundary between Gujarat and Pakistan’s Sindh. The dispute stems from conflicting interpretations of a 1914 British resolution. Pakistan claims the boundary lies on the eastern bank (green line), while India claims it follows the mid-channel (blue dotted line).

questions.q: Q.30) Consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ False Smut: Fungal disease in rice 2️⃣ Leptospirosis: Bacterial infection found in contaminated water 3️⃣ Crohn's disease: Chronic inflammatory bowel disease 4️⃣ Keratoconus: Progressive neurodegenerative disorder
questions.e: False smut is a rice fungal disease caused by Ustilaginoidea virens. Leptospirosis is a bacterial disease transmitted via animal urine in water or soil. Crohn’s is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease. Keratoconus is an eye condition where the cornea thins and bulges, not a neurodegenerative disorder; Parkinson's fits that description. Pairs I, II, and III are correct.

questions.q: Q.31) Consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ PRIP Scheme: Provides 100% funding for all private startups in pharma sector 2️⃣ PM-SETU Scheme: Provides financial support to students for upgrading skills 3️⃣ PM Vishwakarma: Supports artisans with credit and toolkit
questions.e: PM Vishwakarma supports artisans with toolkits (₹15,000 e-vouchers), training stipends (₹500/day), and collateral-free loans. PRIP financial assistance for early projects is 100% only up to ₹1 crore, with 50% for additional costs. PM-SETU modernizes ITIs but does not provide direct financial support or allowances to individual students. Only Pair III is correct.

questions.q: Q.32) With reference to recent military exercises involving India, consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ Drone Kavach: United States 2️⃣ Passage Exercise (PASSEX): Russia 3️⃣ KONKAN-25: United Kingdom 4️⃣ Bold Kurukshetra: Singapore
questions.e: KONKAN-25 is a bilateral maritime exercise with the UK. Bold Kurukshetra 2025 is a joint military exercise with Singapore. Drone Kavach was an internal exercise by the Indian Army’s Spear Corps, not a joint one with the US. The June 2025 PASSEX was conducted with the UK's Royal Navy, not Russia. Pairs III and IV are correct.

questions.q: Q.33) With reference to the Green Sea Turtle, consider the following — 1️⃣ It is categorised as endangered in the IUCN Red List 2️⃣ It is a keystone marine species found in tropical and subtropical waters
questions.e: The Green Sea Turtle's IUCN Red List status improved from Endangered to Least Concern due to sustained conservation efforts. It is a keystone species essential for maintaining coral reefs and seagrass meadows in tropical and subtropical waters. Statement I is thus incorrect.

questions.q: Q.34) Which one of the following rivers forms part of the international boundary between India and Bangladesh?
questions.e: The Ichamati River is a transboundary tidal river shared by West Bengal (India) and Bangladesh. Originating in Nadia district, it flows for 216 km and serves as a vital international boundary and lifeline for local communities. It remains famous for the traditional Durga idol immersion ceremony involving both nations.

questions.q: Q.35) Indian Pangolin is found in which of the following protected areas? — 1️⃣ Kanha Tiger Reserve 2️⃣ Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary 3️⃣ Male Mahadeshwara Hills Wildlife Sanctuary 4️⃣ Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve
questions.e: The Indian Pangolin is widely distributed across various protected areas, including Kanha (Madhya Pradesh), Asola Bhatti (Delhi), Male Mahadeshwara Hills (Karnataka), and Sathyamangalam (Tamil Nadu). These parks support various mammals like tigers, leopards, and gaurs alongside the pangolin.

questions.q: Q.36) Which one of the following is the correct descending order of countries by the size of their official government/central banks gold reserves? — 1️⃣ USA 2️⃣ India 3️⃣ China 4️⃣ Germany
questions.e: As of August 2025, the order is USA (8,133.5 tonnes), Germany (3,350.3 tonnes), China (2,302.3 tonnes), and India (880 tonnes). The USA holds the largest reserves, constituting 78.7% of its total foreign reserves. India ranks ninth globally, with gold accounting for 13.8% of its reserves.

questions.q: Q.37) With reference to the World Commission on Protected Areas (WCPA), consider the following — 1️⃣ It is a technical commission of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) 2️⃣ It presents the Kenton R. Miller Award for impactful innovation in the management of protected areas
questions.e: The WCPA is one of six technical commissions of the IUCN, established in 1948. It presents the Kenton R. Miller Award every two years for innovations in protected area management. In 2025, Sonali Ghosh (Kaziranga Director) became the first Indian recipient of this award.

questions.q: Q.38) 'Steadfast Noon' is an annual nuclear deterrence exercise conducted by which one of the following groups?
questions.e: Steadfast Noon is an annual NATO exercise for training air forces in handling U.S. nuclear weapons stored in Europe. No live weapons are used, but the drills test operational coordination and deterrence strategy. The 2025 exercise was hosted by the Netherlands, primarily at Volkel Air Base.

questions.q: Q.39) "Mera Hou Chongba Festival" belongs to which one of the following States?
questions.e: Mera Hou Chongba is celebrated in Manipur on the 15th lunar day of the Meitei month of Mera. It is the only festival involving all indigenous communities (hill and valley), symbolizing unity and harmony. The titular King leads rituals at Kangla, including an exchange of gifts between tribal chiefs and the royal palace.

questions.q: Q.40) Methamphetamine, sometimes seen in the news, is known for which one of the following characteristics?
o: It is a naturally occurring alkaloid used in traditional medicine.
It is a vaccine developed for the treatment of viral encephalitis.
It is a highly addictive stimulant that affects the central nervous system.
It is a biological pesticide used in organic farming.
questions.e: Methamphetamine is a synthetic stimulant that increases dopamine levels, causing euphoria and alertness. Long-term use results in severe risks like "meth mouth," memory loss, psychosis, and addiction. UNODC reported a record 236 tons seized last year, with 94% occurring in Southeast Asia.

questions.q: Q.41) Consider the following statements regarding Limestone — Statement I: Limestone mine leaseholders in India can sell or utilize limestone for any purpose without regulatory restrictions. Statement II: The Government of India has classified limestone as a major mineral.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: The Centre classified limestone entirely as a major mineral, removing the distinction between minor (kiln use) and major (industrial use) categories. This classification under the MMDR Act allows leaseholders to sell or use it for any purpose without end-use restrictions. Statement II thus explains the freedom noted in Statement I.

questions.q: Q.42) What is Maitri-II, recently seen in the news?
o: It is ISRO's next-generation Earth-observation satellite designed for climate monitoring.
It is India's first automated and remotely operated research base in Antarctica.
It is a newly launched coastal surveillance radar system deployed by the Indian Navy.
It is a high-capacity electric train project being developed under Indian Railways.
questions.e: Maitri-2 is India's fourth planned research station in Antarctica, set to replace the aging Maitri station by 2029. Located in East Antarctica, it will accommodate 90 scientists and use automated instruments to relay data to India even when unmanned. It will support advanced studies in climate change and biodiversity.

questions.q: Q.43) Which one of the following best describes the system of run-off election sometimes mentioned in the context of presidential democracies?
o: It is an election conducted when the parliament decides to dissolve itself before completing its term.
It is an election conducted to fill a vacant legislative seat before the normal term ends.
It is an election held when no candidate secures a majority in the first round of voting.
It is an election held to choose a new leader when the incumbent resigns or is removed from office.
questions.e: A run-off election is a second round of voting between the top two candidates from the first round. It is held only if no candidate achieves the required majority initially. This system is common in presidential republics to ensure the winner has broad support. Recently, opposition leader Herminie won in Seychelles via a runoff.

questions.q: Q.44) Recently, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) published an updated version of the Red List of Threatened Species. In this regard, consider the following — 1️⃣ Over half of all species assessed by the Red List are now classified as 'threatened with extinction' 2️⃣ About 11.5% of bird species assessed are globally threatened, and most species show declining populations
questions.e: The updated Red List includes 172,620 species, of which 48,646 (roughly 28%, not over half) are threatened with extinction. Among 11,185 assessed bird species, 11.5% are globally threatened and 61% show declining populations. Six species, including the Christman Island shrew and slender-billed curlew, were moved to the Extinct category.

questions.q: Q.45) Which of the following countries share land border with Mongolia? — 1️⃣ Russia 2️⃣ China 3️⃣ Kazakhstan 4️⃣ Kyrgyzstan
questions.e: Mongolia is a landlocked country sharing borders only with China and Russia. While Kazakhstan is the next closest nation (only 23 miles away), it does not share a land border. Kyrgyzstan is separated from Mongolia by China. The President of Mongolia visited India in 2025 to mark 70 years of diplomatic ties.

questions.q: Q.46) Consider the following statements with regard to the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021 — 1️⃣ It prohibits commercial surrogacy but permits altruistic surrogacy 2️⃣ The age cap will not apply to couples with frozen embryos before the commencement of the Act
questions.e: The Act permits altruistic surrogacy (no monetary benefit except medical/insurance) to prevent exploitation. It sets age limits: women 23-50 and men 26-55. The Supreme Court recently ruled that these age limits do not apply to couples who froze embryos and started the process before the law took effect on January 25, 2022.

questions.q: Q.47) Consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ Tikhir: Nagaland 2️⃣ Siddi: Gujarat 3️⃣ Soliga: Assam 4️⃣ Kolam: Kerala
questions.e: The Tikhir are an indigenous tribe from Nagaland. Siddis are an Afro-Indian community found in Gujarat, Karnataka, and Goa. Soliga tribes are forest-dwellers in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, not Assam. Kolam tribes reside in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh, not Kerala. Only pairs I and II are correct.

questions.q: Q.48) Which one of the following countries has become the first in the world to achieve 'triple elimination' of mother-to-child transmission of HIV, Syphilis and Hepatitis B?
questions.e: The WHO validated the Maldives for eliminating mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B, adding to its existing validation for HIV and syphilis. This makes it the first country globally to achieve 'triple elimination'. Success was driven by universal testing and near-total antenatal care coverage for pregnant women.

questions.q: Q.49) Consider the following statements — Statement-I: Rhodamine B is widely used in textiles, paper and leather industries. Statement-II: Rhodamine B makes the color durable and more resistant to fading over time.
o: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement-I.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I.
questions.e: Rhodamine B is a synthetic dye used in textiles and leather due to its vivid pink hue and durability against fading. Its water solubility allows for uniform application in industrial processes. While useful industrially, it is toxic if consumed, potentially causing DNA damage and tumors in the liver and bladder.

questions.q: Q.50) Consider the following statements regarding the Somnath temple — 1️⃣ It was built in the traditional Chaulukya style of architecture 2️⃣ It is situated at a Triveni sangam of three rivers - Kapila, Hiran and Sarasvati 3️⃣ Its most recent reconstruction was completed in 1951 by Vallabhbhai Patel
questions.e: Somnath is considered the first of the twelve jyotirlingas. The present temple was reconstructed in the Chaulukya style and completed in May 1951, a project led by Vallabhbhai Patel. It is located at the Triveni sangam, the confluence of the Kapila, Hiran, and Sarasvati rivers.

questions.q: Q.51) The Doctrine of 'SAMADHAN' represents a comprehensive framework of the Government of India to counter:
questions.e: SAMADHAN was formulated by the MHA in 2017 to counter Naxalism. The acronym stands for Smart Leadership, Aggressive Strategy, Motivation, Actionable Intelligence, Dashboard-based KPIs, Harnessing Technology, Action Plan for each theatre, and No access to financing. LWE violence has reduced by over 75% since 2010 due to these principles.

questions.q: Q.52) Which of the following factors are considered by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) while recommending the Minimum Support Price (MSP)? — 1️⃣ Cost of production 2️⃣ Demand-supply situation of various crops 3️⃣ Inter-crop price parity 4️⃣ Terms of trade between the agriculture and non-agriculture sectors 5️⃣ Margin of at least 50% over the cost of production
o: I, II, III, IV and V
questions.e: CACP analyzes costs (A2, A2+FL, C2), market demand-supply, and inter-crop parity to ensure cropping balance. It considers the "terms of trade" to protect farmers' purchasing power relative to the industrial sector. Per 2018 policy, MSP is fixed at a minimum 50% margin over the A2+FL cost of production.

questions.q: Q.53) The Sustainable Aquaculture in Mangrove Ecosystems (SAIME) initiative, recently seen the news, is an initiative by:
questions.e: SAIME was conceptualized by the Nature Environment and Wildlife Society (NEWS), a Kolkata-based NGO. It integrates sustainable aquaculture (crab and fish farming) with mangrove restoration to provide livelihoods and reduce pressure on natural resources. Supported by UNDP, it primarily operates in the Indian Sundarbans of West Bengal.

questions.q: Q.54) With reference to "green crackers" in India, consider the following — 1️⃣ They were developed by the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research - National Environmental Engineering Research Institute 2️⃣ Their manufacturing and sale licenses are granted by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.e: CSIR-NEERI developed green crackers to reduce harmful emissions by replacing barium nitrate with less toxic oxidizers. Licenses for manufacturing and sale are granted by the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) under the DPIIT, not the Environment Ministry. The Supreme Court mandates that only certified green crackers can be used in high-pollution areas.

questions.q: Q.55) With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PM-FME) Scheme, consider the following — 1️⃣ It provides assistance to entrepreneurs only to upgrade existing units 2️⃣ It provides support only to collective entities such as Farmer Producer Organisations and Self-Help Groups 3️⃣ It aims to promote one unique product per district that reflects the district's comparative advantage
questions.e: PM-FME supports both new unit setup and upgrading existing ones. It assists individual entrepreneurs with a 35% credit-linked subsidy (up to ₹10 lakh) as well as collective entities like FPOs and SHGs. The "One District One Product" (ODOP) approach is a key feature to promote local food identities. Only Statement III is correct.

questions.q: Q.56) Consider the following statements — Statement I: As the Southwest Monsoon withdraws, Tamil Nadu, coastal Andhra Pradesh, and parts of Kerala experience rainfall. Statement II: During the post-monsoon period, there is formation of a high-pressure area over the Tibetan-Siberian region.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: As the Southwest Monsoon retreats, the ITCZ shifts south, causing northeasterly winds to pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and rain on India's southeast coast. This is driven by rapid cooling in the north, creating a high-pressure area over the Tibetan-Siberian region that reverses the pressure gradient. Statement II thus explains the wind shift mentioned in Statement I.

questions.q: Q.57) With reference to India's relations with Afghanistan, consider the following — 1️⃣ India does not share a direct land border with Afghanistan 2️⃣ The Zaranj-Delaram Highway and the Salma Dam are infrastructure projects built by India in Afghanistan 3️⃣ India has created an alternative trade and transit route for Afghanistan through the Chabahar Port in Iran
questions.e: Official Indian maps show a 106 km border with Afghanistan through the Wakhan Corridor. India built the Zaranj-Delaram Highway (via the BRO) and the Salma Dam (Afghan-India Friendship Dam) to support reconstruction. India also developed Chabahar Port in Iran to provide Afghanistan a trade route bypassing Pakistan. Statements II and III are correct.

questions.q: Q.58) Consider the following statements with regard to MERCOSUR — 1️⃣ It is a trading bloc in Latin America comprising Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay 2️⃣ India has signed a Free Trade Agreement with the MERCOSUR to eliminate tariffs on most goods and services
questions.e: MERCOSUR was formed in 1991 by Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay to facilitate free movement of goods and services. India signed a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) in 2004, not a full Free Trade Agreement. The PTA grants reciprocal fixed tariff preferences with the long-term goal of creating a free trade area.

questions.q: Q.59) Consider the following statements with regard to Leprosy in India — 1️⃣ It is one of the Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs) 2️⃣ India eliminated leprosy as a public health problem 3️⃣ It is treated through the Multi-Drug Therapy regimen
questions.e: Leprosy is caused by Mycobacterium leprae and is classified as an NTD by the WHO. India eliminated it as a "public health problem" (prevalence <1 per 10,000) in December 2005, though new cases still occur. It is treated using the Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT) regimen, which was introduced nationwide in 1983.

questions.q: Q.60) Consider the following statements about the Food and Agriculture Organisation — 1️⃣ It is a specialised agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger 2️⃣ It provides food aid to improve the nutrition of vulnerable people in times of crisis 3️⃣ It publishes the State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World report
questions.e: FAO is the lead UN agency for technical expertise in food security and agriculture. Food aid in crises is the mandate of the World Food Programme (WFP), not the FAO. FAO’s flagship publications include "The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World" and "The State of Food and Agriculture". Statement II is incorrect.

questions.q: Q.61) Which of the following Indian States or Union Territories have more than one capital? — 1️⃣ Jammu and Kashmir 2️⃣ Himachal Pradesh 3️⃣ Maharashtra 4️⃣ Arunachal Pradesh
questions.e: J&K has Srinagar (summer) and Jammu (winter), a practice revived in 2025. Himachal Pradesh uses Shimla (summer) and Dharamshala (winter) due to extreme cold. Maharashtra’s official capital is Mumbai, but Nagpur is the "second capital" hosting the winter assembly session. Arunachal Pradesh has only one capital, Itanagar.

questions.q: Q.62) With reference to the species of Kurunji, consider the following — 1️⃣ It is known as the flower which makes the Neelgiri hills blue 2️⃣ It is considered an indicator of climate change 3️⃣ It grows primarily in the Eravikulam National Park 4️⃣ It is included under Schedule V of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
questions.e: Kurinji blooms once in 12 years and gives the Nilgiris their blue color. Its blooming cycle is sensitive to temperature and rain, making it a climate change indicator. It grows primarily in Eravikulam National Park and Kurinjimala Sanctuary. It is protected under Schedule III (not Schedule V) of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

questions.q: Q.63) Consider the following statements with reference to the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) — 1️⃣ It is the legal tender issued in a digital form 2️⃣ It is not permitted in cross-border transactions 3️⃣ It is backed by gold reserves
questions.e: CBDC is a digital form of fiat currency and legal tender issued by a central bank. It enables both domestic and cross-border transactions without requiring a third-party bank. Unlike stablecoins backed by assets, CBDC is the sovereign currency itself and is a direct liability of the central bank, not necessarily backed by gold.

questions.q: Q.64) With reference to the Poverty Line in India, which of the following statements are correct? — 1️⃣ The Rangarajan Committee fixed the poverty line based on monthly per capita expenditure 2️⃣ Odisha and Bihar have shown the greatest reduction in poverty among 20 major states over the past decade 3️⃣ The Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) provides the key data used for calculating and updating poverty lines in India
questions.e: The Rangarajan Committee  set monthly per capita expenditure lines of ₹972 (rural) and ₹1,407 (urban). A 2025 RBI study found Odisha and Bihar made the biggest gains in poverty reduction. The NSSO's HCES is the primary data source for estimating consumption and poverty across India.

questions.q: Q.65) A behavioural condition is being increasingly observed among children raised in small, urban nuclear families. The child is overindulged by parents and grandparents, given everything they demand without limits or responsibility. This excessive pampering inhibits emotional growth, makes them unable to handle failure or denial, and often leads to irritability, overconfidence, and difficulty adjusting socially as they grow older. Which of the following syndromes is described here?
questions.e: The Six-Pocket Syndrome involves overpampering by six adults (two parents, four grandparents). Originating in China’s one-child era, it leads to emotional immaturity, entitlement, and poor coping mechanisms. Consequences include social maladaptation and dependence. Correction involves setting boundaries and linking rewards to responsibilities.

questions.q: Q.66) Which of the following statements are correct? — 1️⃣ Electric vehicles (EV) are exempted from paying the road tax 2️⃣ The Government of India has set a target of 50% EV penetration by 2030 3️⃣ PM-E-DRIVE offers targeted incentives to strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities
questions.e: EV benefits in India include road tax exemptions and high subsidies covering nearly 46% of some model prices. The PM-E-DRIVE scheme  provides targeted incentives for e-buses and e-trucks to boost domestic manufacturing. The government target is 30% EV penetration by 2030, not 50%.

questions.q: Q.67) Which key outcome document was adopted at the first ARISE Cities Forum 2025 in New Delhi to advance multilevel urban climate action across the Global South?
o: Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals
questions.e: The ARISE Cities Forum 2025 adopted the Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals. Co-hosted by ICLEI South Asia and NIUA, it united delegates from 60 cities. The declaration aims to advance urban resilience, equity, and climate finance in Global South cities ahead of COP30.

questions.q: Q.68) Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Blackbuck? — 1️⃣ It was reintroduced in the Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary in Chhattisgarh after being locally extinct for nearly 50 years 2️⃣ It gets the highest level of legal protection under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
questions.e: Blackbucks were declared locally extinct in Chhattisgarh in 2017 but were reintroduced to Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary starting in 2021. They are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. Although locally threatened, their global IUCN status is Least Concern.

questions.q: Q.69) Which one of the following bodies/treaties is primarily responsible for the management and oversight of the Species Survival Commission (SSC)?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora
questions.e: The SSC is one of seven expert commissions of the IUCN. It is a network of 10,500 experts providing biodiversity conservation data. This information is the primary feed for the IUCN Red List. In 2025, Vivek Menon became the first Asian to chair the commission.

questions.q: Q.70) With reference to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), 2025, consider the following — 1️⃣ It, for the first time, mapped poor populations' exposure to heat, drought, floods, and air pollution 2️⃣ South Asia has the highest number of multidimensionally poor people exposed to one or more climate hazards
questions.e: The 2025 MPI incorporated mapping of exposure to four climate risks (heat, drought, floods, air pollution) for the first time. South Asia is identified as the most climate-exposed region, with 99.1% of its poor population facing at least one hazard. Globally, 1.1 billion people are multidimensionally poor.

questions.q: Q.71) Consider the following statements about the Prime Minister's Schools for Rising India (PM-SHRI) scheme — 1️⃣ These schools will be showcased as exemplary schools for the implementation of the National Education Policy, 2020 2️⃣ The school infrastructure during non-teaching hours would be used as Common Service Centers 3️⃣ A maximum of two schools will be selected from every block or urban local body
questions.e: PM-SHRI develops 14,500 schools as model NEP 2020 institutions. During non-teaching hours, infrastructure is used as a "Samajik Chetna Kendra" for community activities, not Common Service Centers. A maximum of two schools (one elementary, one secondary) are selected per block or urban body.

questions.q: Q.72) With reference to municipal finances in India, consider the following — 1️⃣ The Constitution of India empowers the Parliament to specify by law matters relating to imposition of taxes by municipalities 2️⃣ After the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST), municipalities lost their taxation power on Entry Tax 3️⃣ The audit of the accounts of the municipalities is done as per the provisions of the State law 4️⃣ Municipal bonds cannot be pledged as a security for repo and reverse repo transactions
questions.e: State Legislatures (not Parliament) specify tax matters for municipalities under Article 243X. GST subsumed Entry Tax (Octroi), a major municipal revenue source. Audits are done per State law according to Article 243Z. In 2025, the Finance Ministry permitted using municipal bonds as security for repo transactions. Statements II and III are correct.

questions.q: Q.73) With reference to the United Nations (UN), which of the statements given below are correct? — 1️⃣ It was created under the Atlantic Charter which aimed to provide collective security 2️⃣ Its principal judicial organ is the International Court of Justice 3️⃣ The "UN75 Declaration" sets out 12 commitments to guide global cooperation over the coming decade
questions.e: UN principles were first laid out in the 1941 Atlantic Charter. The ICJ is the UN's principal judicial organ, established in June 1945. In 2020, the General Assembly adopted the "UN75 Declaration," outlining 12 commitments like digital cooperation and planetary protection for the next decade. The UN turned 80 in 2025.

questions.q: Q.74) The term "Time Rondeau Crystal", frequently seen in news, refers to:
o: A specialized solid-state device used to synchronize atomic clocks across vast geographical distances for satellite navigation systems
An ultra-hard composite crystal developed using nanotechnology to coat aerospace components
A type of photonic crystal designed to slow down light for use in advanced optical communication and quantum computing chips
A state of matter whose component particles exhibit a robust, repeating pattern of motion in time
questions.e: A Time Rondeau Crystal (TRC) is a new phase of matter that repeats in time rather than space. It features a mix of order and randomness, maintaining a repeating pattern over long times while showing irregular motion between those moments. Researchers created one using carbon-13 nuclei in diamond.

questions.q: Q.75) Which one of the following best describes the term Atomic Stencils?
o: A technique to precisely apply polymer patches onto microscopic gold nanoparticles
A position of atoms in an ordered crystal lattice to predict a material's electronic properties
A quantum computing architecture used for parallel processing at the atomic scale
A technique used to create an ultra-fine template for the fabrication of complex integrated circuits on a silicon wafer
questions.e: Atomic stencilling uses a layer of single atoms (like iodide) as a nanoscale mask on a nanoparticle’s surface. This allows scientists to precisely "paint" polymer patches onto gold nanoparticles. The process enables self-assembly of nanoparticles into large 3D crystals called superlattices.

questions.q: Q.76) With reference to the Global Forest Resources Assessment (GFRA), 2025, consider the following — 1️⃣ The total global forest area constitutes roughly 32 per cent of the world's land area 2️⃣ India's total forest area accounts for 2 per cent of the global forest area 3️⃣ Forests globally continue to act as a net carbon sink, absorbing more carbon dioxide than they emit
questions.e: Global forest area is 4.14 billion hectares, covering 32% of total land area. India’s forest area (72 million hectares) represents 2% of the global total, ranking India 9th globally. Despite deforestation, global forests act as a net sink, sequestering roughly 7.8 billion tonnes of CO2 annually.

questions.q: Q.77) The 'State of Finance for Forests 2025' report is released by which one of the following organizations?
questions.e: The UNEP releases the "State of Finance for Forests" report. The 2025 report highlights that forest investment must triple by 2030 to address climate and biodiversity loss. It identifies an annual funding gap of US$216 billion. The FAO releases separate reports like SOFO and the GFRA.

questions.q: Q.78) With reference to the Synchronous All India Elephant Estimation (SAIEE) 2021-25 survey, consider the following — 1️⃣ Elephants have been counted every five years since the launch of Project Elephant in 1992 2️⃣ The Eastern Ghats is the largest landscape for India's elephant population 3️⃣ SAIEE was conducted by the Forest Research Institute
questions.e: Elephant censuses have been conducted every five years since 1992. The Western Ghats (not Eastern) is the largest landscape, hosting over 53% of the population. The survey was conducted by the Environment Ministry, Project Elephant, and the Wildlife Institute of India, not the FRI. Only Statement I is correct.

questions.q: Q.79) What is the '#23for23 Initiative', recently seen in the news?
o: It mandates planting 23 trees per household to mark International Snow Leopard Day.
It requires companies to sponsor 23 community forest patrol teams annually for snow leopard habitats.
It is a financial incentive scheme offering 23,000 to rural households for wildlife protection.
It encourages people to undertake physical activity for 23 minutes to raise awareness about snow leopard conservation.
questions.e: Launched by the MoEFCC on International Snow Leopard Day (23 Oct), this campaign encourages 23 minutes of physical activity to raise awareness for snow leopard conservation. The number serves as a mnemonic for the date. India’s first national snow leopard census estimated 718 individuals, with 477 found in Ladakh.

questions.q: Q.80) Consider the following statements about the National Biodiversity Authority — 1️⃣ It is a statutory body established under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 2️⃣ It grants prior approval for all Intellectual Property Rights that are based on Indian biological resources 3️⃣ It assesses and notifies the areas of biodiversity importance as Biodiversity Heritage Sites
questions.e: The NBA is a statutory body established in 2003 under the Biological Diversity Act 2002, not the Wildlife Act. It must approve IPR applications based on Indian biological resources to prevent biopiracy. Biodiversity Heritage Sites are notified by State Governments, not the NBA. Only Statement II is correct, so I and III are not correct.

questions.q: Q.81) With reference to cloud seeding, consider the following — Statement I: Cloud seeding efforts during the post-monsoon season are unlikely to yield significant rainfall. Statement II: During the post-monsoon season, atmospheric conditions largely favour dry weather conditions and depressions are largely absent.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
questions.e: Post-monsoon cloud seeding (Oct-Dec) is unlikely to succeed because moisture-laden monsoon clouds and low-pressure systems are absent. Atmospheric conditions during this time favor dry weather unless triggered by western disturbances. Statement II correctly identifies the meteorological conditions that make seeding in Statement I unfeasible.

questions.q: Q.82) With reference to Geothermal Energy, consider the following — 1️⃣ High-enthalpy resources associated with volcanic regions, geysers and hot springs are used for electricity generation 2️⃣ Unreliable baseload supply and suppressed grid stability are the main disadvantages of geothermal power 3️⃣ The Geological Survey of India has identified Andaman Nicobar Islands and Son-Narmada-Tapi as geothermal provinces
questions.e: High-enthalpy volcanic resources generate electricity, while low-enthalpy resources serve direct uses like heating. Geothermal power provides 24/7 reliable baseload supply and enhances grid stability, which are advantages, not disadvantages. GSI identified 10 provinces including SONATA and the Andaman Nicobar Islands. Statements I and III are correct.

questions.q: Q.83) Which one of the following is not correct with regard to the Goods and Services Tax regime?
o: Centre and States agreed to have concurrent power to tax goods and services.
The GST revenue has consistently increased since its implementation in 2017.
The Constitution confers on both the Union and State, the concurrent jurisdiction to levy tax on supply of goods and services.
GST Law Committee proposes changes in the GST laws taking into account various feedbacks.
questions.e: GST revenue has seen fluctuations, such as a notable dip in the 2020-21 fiscal year (averaging ₹94,734 crore) compared to 2019-20. The 101st Amendment and Article 246A preserved federalism by conferring concurrent taxing powers to both the Union and States. The GST Law Committee proposes reforms like rate rationalization.

questions.q: Q.84) Which of the following statements is/are correct? — 1️⃣ Blockchain functions like a ledger of records or transactions, resistant to tampering and accessible across a network of computers 2️⃣ Vishvasya Blockchain Stack provides the technical foundation for building and deploying blockchain-based applications for governance 3️⃣ Praamaanik is a solution that leverages blockchain technology to verify the authenticity and source of mobile applications
questions.e: Blockchain is a secure, immutable ledger accessible across a network. The National Blockchain Framework uses the Vishvasya Blockchain Stack as its indigenous platform for building governance applications. Praamaanik uses blockchain records to verify the legitimacy and source of mobile apps to protect against fraudulent software.

questions.q: Q.85) Recently, the Government of India released a ₹200 commemorative coin to mark which one of the following historic events?
o: 200 Years of Mysore's First War of Independence
200 Years of Rani Chennamma's Victory at Kittur
questions.e: In October 2025, the Ministry of Culture commemorated 200 years of Rani Chennamma’s victory at Kittur . To honor her legacy as one of India's earliest female freedom fighters, a ₹200 commemorative coin was released. Her resistance predated the 1857 Revolt and inspired future generations.

questions.q: Q.86) With reference to protected sites in India, consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ Khangchendzonga National Park: Arunachal Pradesh 2️⃣ Changthang Wildlife Sanctuaries: Ladakh 3️⃣ Nangal Wildlife Sanctuary: Orissa 4️⃣ Bondla Wildlife Sanctuary: Goa
questions.e: Khangchendzonga National Park is in Sikkim, not Arunachal Pradesh. Changthang is in Ladakh. Nangal Wildlife Sanctuary is in Punjab, not Orissa. Bondla is in Goa. Only pairs II and IV are correctly matched.

questions.q: Q.87) Consider the following statements about the Rehabilitation Council of India — 1️⃣ It is a statutory body established under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 2️⃣ It regulates access to the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) platform by Persons with Disabilities (PWD)
questions.e: The RCI is a statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, not Health. Its mandate is to regulate services for PWDs, standardize syllabi, and maintain the Central Rehabilitation Register. It does not specifically regulate ABDM platform access. Statement II is incorrect.

questions.q: Q.88) With reference to India's 6G Vision 2030, consider the following — 1️⃣ 6G aims to send and receive information in just 5-10 millisecond 2️⃣ The Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) has been formed to foster indigenous research 3️⃣ It aims to create a sector contributing nearly USD 1.2 trillion to the national GDP by 2035
questions.e: 6G aims for 1 microsecond latency, which is 1,000 times faster than 5G; 5-10 milliseconds is 4G speed. The B6GA fosters indigenous research and international collaboration. The 6G roadmap envisions the sector contributing $1.2 trillion to GDP by 2035. Statements II and III are correct.

questions.q: Q.89) Consider the following statements with regard to Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in Delhi NCR — 1️⃣ It is operationalized only when air quality is classified as 'Severe' or 'Severe Plus' as per the Air Quality Index 2️⃣ Measures imposed under the previous categories continue even when the subsequent category measures are activated 3️⃣ It is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.e: GRAP Stage 1 activates when AQI is 'poor' (201–300). Subsequent stages activate before reaching 'very poor,' 'severe,' and 'severe plus'. Measures from lower stages continue when higher stages are triggered. It is implemented by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), not the Ministry directly. Only Statement II is correct.

questions.q: Q.90) The term 'Willow', recently in the news, refers to:
questions.e: Willow is Google Quantum AI's next-generation processor. In 2025, it demonstrated quantum advantage by outperforming supercomputers on complex problems. It successfully executed a Decoded Quantum Interferometry algorithm for solving optimization problems and studied information scrambling.

questions.q: Q.91) With reference to India's maritime strength, consider the following — 1️⃣ India currently handles about 10% of global seaborne trade 2️⃣ About 50% of India's maritime trade cargo is carried on India-owned vessels 3️⃣ The Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 aims to expand India's total port-handling capacity to 10,000 MMTA
questions.e: India currently handles 10% of global seaborne trade. Only about 20% (not 50%) of trade cargo is carried on India-flagged or owned vessels. The MIV 2047 aims for a fourfold expansion of port capacity to 10,000 MMTPA. Statements I and III are correct.

questions.q: Q.92) Consider the following statements about the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar 2025 — 1️⃣ It is India's highest recognition for exemplary and inspirational contributions in the fields of science, technology, and innovation 2️⃣ The Vigyan Yuva - Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award acknowledges young scientists below 45 years 3️⃣ These cannot be given posthumously
questions.e: The Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar is the nation's highest scientific honor. The Vigyan Yuva-SSB award targets scientists up to age 45. Awards can be given posthumously; for example, Prof. Jayant Vishnu Narlikar received the 2025 Vigyan Ratna posthumously. Statement III is incorrect.

questions.q: Q.93) There are deep learning models trained on immense amounts of data, making them capable of understanding and generating natural language and other types of content to perform a wide range of tasks. They work as giant statistical prediction machines that repeatedly predict the next word in a sequence. They learn patterns in their text and generate language that follows those patterns. When given agentic capabilities, they can perform, with varying degrees of autonomy, various tasks that would otherwise be performed by humans. They are the culmination of decades of progress in Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning research, and their development is largely responsible for the explosion of artificial intelligence advancements across the late 2010s and 2020s. In the context of emerging technologies, which of the following terms best applies to the above scenario?
questions.e: Large Language Models (LLMs) are deep learning models trained on massive data for varied tasks. They use transformer architecture to predict the next word in a sequence based on learned patterns. LLMs can adapt to summarize text, debug code, or act as agents. Examples include Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude.

questions.q: Q.94) Which of the following statements are correct about the India-ASEAN partnership? — 1️⃣ India has accorded 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership' to its relation with ASEAN 2️⃣ India is part of the East Asian Summit, an ASEAN-led framework 3️⃣ ASEAN remained the second largest trading partner of India in 2024-25 4️⃣ The year 2026 has been designated as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation
questions.e: India's relation with ASEAN is a 'Comprehensive Strategic Partnership'; 'Special and Privileged' is the term used for Russia. India participates in the East Asian Summit. ASEAN was the 2nd largest partner in 2023-24, but 2024-25 data shows the US first and China second. 2026 is designated the Year of Maritime Cooperation.

questions.q: Q.95) Consider the following — 1️⃣ Money Laundering 2️⃣ Sale or purchase of passwords 3️⃣ Interception of non-public data transmissions 4️⃣ Online distribution of child pornography
questions.e: The UN Convention against Cybercrime covers laundering proceeds from cybercrimes. It criminalizes the sale or purchase of login details for hacking. It prohibits the interception of non-public data transmissions. It specifically strengthens tools to fight online child sexual abuse material (CSAM). All four are covered.

questions.q: Q.96) With reference to the 'Global Virus Network (GVN)', consider the following — 1️⃣ It is a network of countries most affected by the Corona virus pandemic to advance knowledge about viruses 2️⃣ It has launched the Global Guardians initiative to train young people in pandemic preparedness
questions.e: GVN is a global coalition of virologists, not just affected countries, working on diagnostics and vaccines. "Global Guardians: Youth for Pandemic Preparedness" is their initiative to train students in the science of pandemics and vaccines. Multiple Indian institutes, like the Institute of Advanced Virology, are members.

questions.q: Q.97) In the context of defence, the METEOR is:
questions.e: Meteor is a next-generation BVRAAM developed by the European consortium MBDA. It uses ramjet propulsion to maintain high speeds and has a range exceeding 150 km. Its "no-escape zone" is significantly larger than other missiles, making evasion nearly impossible once engaged.

questions.q: Q.98) The term Axial Seamount, recently seen in the news, refers to:
o: a seamount chain in the Arctic Ocean
a submarine volcano located in the Pacific Ocean
a volcanic island in the Indian Ocean near Indonesia
the highest volcanic peak in the Andes Mountains
questions.e: Axial Seamount is an active submarine volcano on the Juan de Fuca Ridge in the northeast Pacific, 480 km off the US coast. It sits on a hotspot where magma rises through tectonic boundaries. Real-time monitoring in 2025 revealed signs of renewed volcanic activity.

questions.q: Q.99) With reference to the Bordetella holmesii, recently seen the news, consider the following statements:
o: It is a lesser known bacteria that can cause whooping-type symptoms and chest infections.
It is a newly discovered bacteria that is associated with tuberculosis.
It is responsible for leakage in the gut and weakening the immune system.
questions.e: A PGIMER study found that B. holmesii is responsible for a substantial fraction of pertussis-like (whooping cough) illnesses in North Indian children. It mimics the clinical picture of B. pertussis, potentially leading to misdiagnosis. Its rise suggests that current diagnostic and control protocols may need revision.

questions.q: Q.100) "MeghRaj 2.0", recently in the news, refers to:
o: a weather prediction model developed by the IMD
a new Indian Navy communication satellite system
an artificial intelligence platform for agriculture forecasting
questions.e: MeghRaj 2.0 is an upgraded version of India's GI Cloud initiative launched by MeitY. It provides a secure cloud environment for hosting government applications and data. It integrates AI, data analytics, and cybersecurity tools to improve digital service delivery across ministries.
